He tried to remember all the good times he had. He tried to remember the sound of his axe hitting the tree and the smell of the wood chips. He remembered feeling super strong when he used his axe. 

The woodcutter became even more sad a few days later. He had to get a new axe and it wasn't the same. But then he realized the new axe was making him even stronger! 

He now remembers his old axe, but it made him sad. So now he chooses to remember the times with his new axe that make him strong and happy.

The old man smiles. He says, "Thank you, children. I forgive you. You are honest and brave. You can keep the pirate hat and the pirate sword. They are my gift to you. But remember, the real treasure is not in things, but in people. The real pirates are not those who take, but those who share. Will you share your pirate games with me?"

Tom and Mia nod. They say, "Yes, sir. We will share our pirate games with you. You can be our pirate friend. Come, let's play together!"

The old man laughs. He says, "Arrr, mateys, let's go! I have some stories to tell you about my adventures on the sea!"

They all go to the big ship and have fun. They learn to be kind and generous. They are happy. They are the best pirates ever.

Lily liked to play with her toy dragon. She named him Max and pretended he could fly and breathe fire. She wished he was real and big, so they could have more fun together.

One day, she found a shiny stone in the garden. It was cold and smooth, and had a strange mark on it. She thought it was pretty, so she put it in her pocket and took it to her room. She showed it to Max and said, "Look, Max, I found a magic stone for you. Maybe it will make you grow!"

She put the stone next to Max on her bed and went to have dinner. When she came back, she was surprised to see that Max was not on her bed. Instead, there was a hole in the wall and a trail of smoke. She heard a loud roar outside and ran to the window. She saw Max flying in the sky, but he was not a toy anymore. He was a real dragon, and he was huge!

"Max, Max, come back!" Lily shouted. She was happy to see him grow, but she was also scared. She did not know if he would remember her or if he would hurt anyone.

Max heard her voice and turned around. He flew back to the window and looked at Lily with his big, yellow eyes. He snorted and licked her face with his warm tongue. He was still her friend, and he wanted to play with her.

"Lily, you gave me a magic stone. Thank you, thank you!" Max said in a deep voice. He could talk now, too.

Lily smiled and hugged his scaly neck. She was glad he was happy, but she also wondered what to do. She could not keep him in her room anymore, and he could not stay in the garden. He was too big and too loud.

"Max, I love you, but you can't stay here. You need a bigger place, where you can fly and breathe fire. Where you can find other dragons like you. Do you understand?" Lily said in a sad voice.

Max nodded and nuzzled her cheek. He understood, but he did not want to leave her. He wanted to stay with her forever.

"Lily, I love you, too. But you are right. I need a bigger place. But I will always remember you. And I will come back to visit you. I promise. Can you come with me for a ride?" Max said in a hopeful voice.

Lily nodded and climbed on his back. She held on to his horns and felt the wind in her hair. He flew high and fast, and showed her the world. He showed her the mountains and the forests and the lakes. He showed her the stars and the moon and the clouds. He showed her how to grow and be free.

They flew for a long time, until they saw a cave. It was dark and cold, but it was big enough for Max. He landed and let Lily down. He said, "This is my new home. Do you like it?"

Lily looked around and said, "It's nice, Max. But it's not as nice as you. I will miss you, Max. Can I come back to see you?"

Max smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. You can come back anytime. I will always be here for you. You are my best friend. And you are the one who made me grow."

They hugged and said goodbye. Lily walked back to the garden, where her parents were waiting for her. They were worried and angry, but they were also amazed and proud. They saw what Lily had done, and they knew she was special.

Lily told them everything, and they listened and hugged her. They said, "We love you, Lily. And we are happy for you and Max. But you have to be careful. Not everyone will understand. Not everyone will be kind. You have to keep this a secret. Can you do that?"

Lily nodded and said, "I can do that. I can keep a secret. But I can also grow. And I can also be free. Just like Max."

Sara loved yogurt. She ate it every morning with her spoon. She liked all kinds of yogurt: plain, strawberry, banana, peach. But today, she had a problem. Her mom gave her a new yogurt that she had never seen before. It was green and had bits of something in it.

"What is this, mom?" Sara asked, looking at the yogurt with a troubled face.

"It's kiwi yogurt, Sara. It's very yummy and healthy. Try it, you might like it," her mom said, smiling.

Sara took a small bite of the yogurt. She did not like it at all. It was sour and bitter and had seeds that got stuck in her teeth. She made a face and spit it out.

"Yuck! I don't like this yogurt, mom. It's bad. I want a different yogurt," Sara complained, pushing the bowl away.

"Come on, Sara, don't be so picky. You have to eat something for breakfast. You can't waste food. Give it another chance, maybe it will grow on you," her mom said, trying to be patient.

"No, no, no! I don't want this yogurt. I want strawberry yogurt. Strawberry yogurt is good. This yogurt is icky. Please, mom, please, can I have strawberry yogurt?" Sara begged, making a sad face.

Her mom sighed. She knew Sara was a fussy eater, but she also wanted her to try new things and not be wasteful. She decided to make a deal with her.

"Okay, Sara, how about this: if you eat half of this yogurt, I will give you a small cup of strawberry yogurt as a treat. But you have to eat at least half, no less. Deal?" her mom said, holding out her hand.

Sara thought about it. She really wanted strawberry yogurt, but she also really hated kiwi yogurt. She looked at the green bowl and then at her mom's hand. She decided to take the deal.

"Deal," she said, shaking her mom's hand.

She picked up her spoon and ate the yogurt as fast as she could, making faces and noises. She tried not to taste it too much. She counted the bites in her head. One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight. She was done. She showed her mom the empty half of the bowl.

"See, mom, I ate half. Can I have strawberry yogurt now?" she asked, hoping her mom would keep her promise.

Her mom smiled and nodded. She was proud of Sara for trying something new, even if she didn't like it. She got a small cup of strawberry yogurt from the fridge and gave it to Sara.

"Here you go, Sara. You earned it. Good job, sweetie," she said, kissing her on the cheek.

Sara smiled and thanked her mom. She opened the cup and ate the strawberry yogurt with delight. It was sweet and creamy and had no seeds. She liked it a lot. She decided that maybe trying new things was not so bad, as long as she got her favorite yogurt afterwards.

Her mom said, "No, Lily. We can't keep the octopus. It needs to go back to the ocean."

Lily was sad, but she knew her mom was right. She gently squeezed the octopus and put it back in the water. As she watched it swim away, Lily felt happy that she did the right thing. She also learned that even though something might seem cheap or easy to keep, it's important to think about what's best for it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the woods near her house. One day, she found a piece of rope with a big knot in it.

Lily asked her mom, "What is this knot?" Her mom explained that a knot is when the rope gets twisted and tangled together. Lily was curious and wanted to know more about knots.

As she was playing with the rope, she noticed that it was starting to get weak and fray. She said to herself, "I know this rope is not strong anymore." 

Lily decided to go back to her house and show her mom the rope. She said, "Mom, look at this rope. It has a knot and it's weak. Can we fix it?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course we can! Let's work together to untie the knot and make the rope strong again." And so, they spent the afternoon working on the rope and soon it was good as new. Lily was happy to have learned about knots and how to fix them with her mom's help.

The boy was very happy and thanked Lily for helping him. Lily felt good because she told the truth and helped someone in need. She painted a picture of the boy and his truck to remember their adventure. From that day on, Lily knew that helping others was the best thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a tall giraffe named Jerry. Jerry was walking in the jungle when he met a little bird named Lily. 

"Hi Jerry!" said Lily. "What are you doing?"

"I'm just walking around," replied Jerry. "What about you?"

"I'm looking for some steel to build my nest," said Lily. "Do you know where I can find some?"

Jerry thought for a moment and then said, "I think I saw some sharp steel over by the river. But be careful, it's dangerous."

Lily thanked Jerry and flew off to find the steel. When she got there, she saw that the steel was indeed sharp. She remembered what Jerry had said and was careful not to hurt herself. She used the steel to build a strong nest for her family.

The moral of the story is that even though something may be sharp or dangerous, if you are careful and use it wisely, it can be very helpful.

When he was sure that he had enough, he carefully closed the window, while still trying not to let the fog escape. When he looked at his hands, he was amazed to see that he had caught the fog! Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she met a new friend named Max. Max was a big, furry dog who loved to play fetch. Lily was a little scared of Max at first, but he wagged his tail and licked her hand to say hello.

Lily's shadow followed her wherever she went, even when she played with Max. Max didn't seem to mind her shadow, so Lily introduced her shadow to Max. Max sniffed at the shadow and wagged his tail again. Lily giggled and felt happy that her new friend liked her shadow too.

After playing for a while, it was time for Lily to go home. She waved goodbye to Max and promised to come back and play again soon. As she walked home, her shadow followed her, and Lily felt happy knowing that her shadow had a new friend too.

When they got home, Lily was tired from all the fun they had at the park. She went to bed early so she could rest up for the next day's adventures.

Benny said to Timmy, "I want to join but I must resist eating too many carrots." Timmy replied, "But Benny, everyone in the network eats carrots all the time. Don't you want to be like them?" 

Benny thought about it for a moment and then said, "No, I don't want to be like them if it means going against what my mom taught me. I will still be your friend but I won't join the network." 

Timmy respected Benny's decision and they continued to play together. Benny learned that it's important to resist peer pressure and always listen to his mom's advice.

Tim's friend, Sam, saw that Tim was sad. Sam wanted to help. Sam found a way to fix Tim's guitar. Tim was so happy. Now, Tim could play his guitar again. Even though he was deaf, he could still make music and feel happy.

Lily and Timmy played games inside and had a lot of fun. Lily learned that even though she couldn't do what she wanted, she could still have fun and be happy. The moral of the story is that sometimes we can't do what we want, but we can still find joy in other things.

The moral of the story is that if you keep doing what you love, good things will come to you. Even when it's cold outside, keep playing your violin and smile. You never know who might be listening and what wonderful surprises might come your way.

When they get to the zoo, Mom and Dad take them to a special place. They see a sign that says "Rare Animals". They see some animals they have never seen before, like a panda, a koala, and a sloth. They are very cute and soft. Mom and Dad say they can open the box now. Lily and Sam tear off the bow and the paper. Inside the box, they find two stuffed animals. One is a giraffe, and one is a lion. They are very happy and hug them. Mom and Dad say they are special gifts, because they are rare animals too. They wrap them in their arms and thank Mom and Dad. They have a great day at the zoo with their new friends.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bus. The bus has many colors and pictures. The bus says "Circus".

"Look, Sara, a circus!" Tom says. "Let's go and see the animals and clowns!"

Sara and Tom run to the bus. They see a man with a hat. The man has tickets in his hand. He smiles at Sara and Tom.

"Hello, kids, do you want to see the circus?" the man says. "I have two tickets for you. They are free. Just get on the bus and I will take you there."

Sara and Tom are happy. They love the circus. They take the tickets and get on the bus. The man closes the door and drives away.

But the bus does not go to the circus. The bus goes to a dark and scary place. There are no animals or clowns. There are only cages and chains. The man is not nice. He is bad. He wants to sell Sara and Tom to bad people.

Sara and Tom are scared. They cry and scream. They want to go home. They want their mom and dad.

"Help, help, someone help us!" Sara and Tom call. But no one hears them. No one comes. The man laughs and says, "Too late, kids, you are mine now. You should not have taken the tickets. You should not have trusted me."

Sara and Tom are very sad. They wish they never saw the bus. They wish they never met the man. They wish they stayed in the park. They wish they listened to their mom and dad. But it is too late. They are trapped. They are alone. They are afraid. The end.

Anna liked to play with her dolls in the bathtub. She had a big doll with yellow hair and a small doll with brown hair. She pretended they were sisters who went to the beach. She used soap to make bubbles and foam for them.

"Look, Lily, the water is so blue and shiny!" Anna said to the big doll.

"Yes, Anna, it is very pretty. But we have to be careful not to get soap in our eyes. It hurts a lot!" Lily said to Anna.

Anna nodded. She knew that soap was good for cleaning, but not for eyes. She used a cup to rinse the soap off her dolls. She smiled when she saw them sparkle.

Suddenly, she heard a knock on the door. It was her mom.

"Anna, it's time to get out of the bath. You have been in there for a long time. You don't want to get wrinkly, do you?" Mom said.

Anna frowned. She did not want to stop playing. She liked the bath.

"Can I stay a little longer, Mom? Please?" Anna asked.

Mom shook her head. She opened the door and saw the bathtub full of bubbles and foam. She also saw something else. She recognized it right away. It was her new soap. The one that smelled like roses and cost a lot of money.

"Anna, what did you do? That's my soap! You used all of it!" Mom said.

Anna looked at the soap. It was very small and thin. She did not know it was Mom's soap. She thought it was for everyone.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I didn't know. I just wanted to make bubbles and foam for my dolls. They liked it a lot. See?" Anna said.

She held up her dolls to show Mom. They were covered in bubbles and foam. They looked happy.

Mom sighed. She was angry, but she also felt sorry for Anna. She knew Anna did not mean to be bad. She just wanted to have fun.

"It's okay, Anna. I forgive you. But next time, you have to ask me before you use my soap. And you have to use less of it. Soap is not a toy. It is for washing. Do you understand?" Mom said.

Anna nodded. She understood. She felt bad for making Mom angry. She wanted to make Mom happy.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I love you. Can I give you a hug?" Anna said.

Mom smiled. She loved Anna too. She bent down and gave Anna a hug. She felt the bubbles and foam on Anna's skin. They tickled her nose.

"Of course, you can, Anna. I love you too. But you are very wet and soapy. You need to dry off and put on your pajamas. Come on, let's go. And be careful, don't slip. You have to walk slow." Mom said.

Anna got out of the bathtub. She wrapped herself in a towel. She followed Mom to her bedroom. She walked slow. She did not want to fall. She was happy Mom was not angry anymore. She was happy she had her dolls. She was happy she had bubbles and foam. She was happy she had soap. Even if it was Mom's soap.

Tom and Sue were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a stream near their house. The stream had clear water and many fish. Tom and Sue wanted to catch some fish with their hands.

They ran to the stream and dipped their hands in the water. They tried to grab the fish, but the fish were too fast and slippery. Tom and Sue laughed and splashed each other.

"Look, there is a big fish over there!" Tom said, pointing to a dark spot in the water.

"Let's catch it!" Sue said, and ran to the other side of the stream.

But the dark spot was not a fish. It was a smelly pipe that poured dirty water into the stream. The dirty water made bubbles and foam and smelled bad.

Sue did not see the pipe. She stepped on it and slipped. She fell into the dirty water and screamed.

"Help, help!" Sue cried. "The water is smelly and hurts my eyes!"

Tom heard Sue and ran to help her. But the stream was too wide and deep. He could not reach Sue. He saw Sue's head go under the water and then come up again.

"Sue, Sue, hold on!" Tom shouted. "I will get help!"

Tom ran to their house and called their mom. Their mom came with Tom to the stream. But it was too late. Sue was gone. The dirty water had taken her away.

Tom and Sue were separated. Tom was very sad. He wished he had never seen the stream. He wished he had stayed with Sue. He wished he could see Sue again.

Sam and Mia are confused. They think the new boy is rude. They do not want to be his friend anymore. They go back to their snowballs and snowmen.

Soon, a man came to pick up the box. He lifted it and carried it to his truck. Lily felt the box move. She was scared. She tried to call for help, but no one heard her. She wished she had listened to her teacher and left school with her friends. She learned a hard lesson.

Tom was angry and said, "That car is not special. It is just a toy. I have a better car at home. It is blue and shiny and has a remote control. I will give you my car if you give me your car. That is a fair price."

Tom was more angry and said, "Fine. You are mean and selfish. I do not want to be your friend. I will find another car to play with." He stomped away and left Anna and Ben alone.

Anna and Ben hugged each other and smiled. They did not care what Tom said. They knew their car was special and they were happy to have it. They played with their car and had fun. They thanked grandma for their gift and said they loved her.

Lily wanted to play with the plastic cups and plates in the kitchen. She liked to pretend she was having a tea party with her dolls and stuffed animals. She asked her mom if she could use them.

"Mom, can I play with the plastic things?" Lily said.

"Hello, everyone, welcome to my tea party. I have some yummy snacks for you. Do you like spicy food?" Lily said.

She gave each of her guests a plastic plate with a cracker and a slice of cheese. She poured some water into the plastic cups and added some red sauce from a bottle.

"This is ketchup. It is spicy and tasty. Do you want some?" Lily said.

She put some ketchup on her cracker and cheese and took a bite. She made a face and spit it out.

"Yuck! This is too spicy for me. I don't like it. Do you like it?" Lily said.

She looked at her dolls and stuffed animals. They did not say anything. They did not eat their food. They looked unhappy.

"Maybe you don't like spicy food either. I'm sorry. I will get you something else. Do you want some cookies or fruit?" Lily said.

She ran to the kitchen to find something else for her guests. She hoped they would not be mad at her. She wanted them to have fun at her tea party. She loved them very much.

"Look, Kim, an otter!" Tim said. "It has a fish. I want a fish too. Let's catch one."

"No, Tim, we can't catch a fish. That's not nice. The fish are the otter's friends. We have to listen to mom and dad. They said we can't touch the animals or their food." Kim said.

But Tim did not listen to Kim. He ran to the river and tried to grab a fish with his hands. He splashed and shouted, but the fish were too fast and slippery. He got wet and cold and angry.

The otter heard Tim and did not like him. The otter thought Tim was rude and mean. The otter swam to Tim and bit his finger. Tim cried out in pain and let go of the fish. The otter took the fish and swam away.

"Ow, ow, ow! The otter bit me! It hurts!" Tim said.

"Tim, I told you not to catch a fish. You should have listened to me and mom and dad. The otter was just protecting its food. You have to be kind and gentle to the animals. They have feelings too." Kim said.

She hugged Tim and helped him dry his finger. She gave him a band-aid and a cookie. Tim said he was sorry and learned his lesson. He said he would never bother the otter or the fish again. He said he would listen to Kim and mom and dad. He said he liked the cookie. It was delicious.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big red strawberry on a plant. Lily wanted to eat it, but Ben said they should ask first.

"Who cares?" Lily said. "It looks yummy. I want it now."

She picked the strawberry and took a big bite. It was sweet and juicy. She smiled and said, "Mmm, this is the best strawberry ever. You should try it, Ben."

Ben shook his head. He knew that the strawberry belonged to Mrs. Green, the old lady who lived next door. She was very kind and often gave them cookies and milk. He said, "No, thank you. I think we should put it back. Mrs. Green will be sad if she sees it gone."

Lily laughed. She thought Ben was silly and scared. She said, "Don't be a baby. She won't notice. And if she does, she won't mind. She has many strawberries. Come on, have some. It's fun."

She took another bite and offered the rest to Ben. Ben felt bad. He wanted to be a good friend, but he also wanted to be honest. He said, "No, Lily. I don't want it. I think we should say sorry to Mrs. Green and give her something nice. Maybe some flowers or a card."

Lily liked to observe things. She liked to look at the sky, the trees, the birds, and the bugs. She liked to see how they moved and what they did. She had a big book with pictures of many things. She liked to learn their names and sounds.

One day, Lily found a toy car in her brother's room. It was red and shiny and had four wheels. She wanted to play with it. She pushed a button on the car, but nothing happened. She pushed it again and again, but still nothing. She was sad. She wondered why the car did not work.

She looked at the car more closely. She saw a small door on the bottom of the car. She opened it and saw two round things inside. They looked like the things in her flashlight. She remembered that her flashlight needed those things to make light. She thought that maybe the car needed them too.

She took the two round things out of the car and went to find her flashlight. She opened the flashlight and saw that it had two round things too. She swapped them with the ones from the car. They heard a loud noise. It was a dog. It was barking and running towards the pit. It was a big and scary dog. It wanted to get the coin.

"Run, run!" Sam said.

Lily grabbed a stick and hit the dog. The dog let go of Sam's leg and ran away. Lily helped Sam out of the pit.

"Are you OK, Sam?" Lily said.

"No, it hurts!" Sam said. He showed Lily his leg. It was bleeding.

"Let's go home and tell Mom!" Lily said.

"OK, but don't tell her about the pit!" Sam said.

They walked home, holding hands. They learned a serious lesson. They should not go into pits. They should stay away from dogs. They should listen to Mom.

Ben hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry you drank soap. Mommy will help you. Let's go find her." He took Lily's hand and they ran to the living room. They saw Mommy sitting on the couch and reading a book. They screamed, "Mommy, Mommy, help!"

Mommy heard them and looked up. She saw their faces and the soap on the plate. She said, "Oh, my poor babies. What happened?" She put down her book and took them in her arms. She said, "Did you drink soap? That is very bad. You have to rinse your mouth with clean water. Come on, let's go to the bathroom."

She carried them to the bathroom and turned on the faucet. She gave them each a cup of water and told them to rinse their mouth and spit. She said, "This will make you feel better. Soap is not for drinking. It is for washing dishes and hands. You have to be careful with what you put in your mouth. Do you understand?"

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, Mommy. We're sorry. We won't drink soap again. We love you."

Mommy kissed them and said, "I love you too. You are my sweet babies. Now, how about we make a real cake together? Would you like that?"

Lily and Ben smiled and said, "Yes, Mommy. We would like that very much." They hugged Mommy and followed her to the kitchen. They forgot about the soap and looked forward to the cake. They were happy again.

Tom and Sam were brothers who liked to play on the farm. They had many animals, but their favorite was Molly the mule. Molly was very strong and could carry heavy things, but she was also very slow and stubborn. Sometimes she would stop and not move, no matter how much Tom and Sam pulled or pushed.

One day, Tom and Sam wanted to go to the pond and catch some frogs. They decided to take Molly with them, so they could ride on her back. They put a saddle and a bridle on Molly and climbed on. "Come on, Molly, let's go!" Tom said, holding the reins. "We want to see the frogs!"

But Molly did not want to go. She shook her head and snorted. She did not like the pond, because it was wet and muddy. She liked to stay in the barn, where it was dry and cozy. She dug her hooves into the ground and refused to budge.

"Please, Molly, please!" Sam begged, patting her neck. "It will be fun, we promise! We will give you a carrot when we come back!"

But Molly did not care. She was happy where she was. She ignored Tom and Sam and started to munch on some hay.

Tom and Sam were getting frustrated. They did not know what to do. They looked around and saw their dad working in the field. He was driving a big tractor that made a loud noise. He was plowing the soil and making rows for the seeds.

"Hey, dad!" Tom shouted, waving his hand. "Can you help us? Molly won't move!"

Their dad looked up and saw them. He smiled and waved back. He drove the tractor closer to them and stopped. He got off and walked over to Molly. He stroked her ears and whispered something in her ear.

"Molly, you have to listen to Tom and Sam," he said. "They are your friends and they want to have fun with you. The pond is not so bad, it's cool and refreshing. And there are many things to see and hear. You might even like it. But if you don't go, you will miss out on a lot of fun. And you will make Tom and Sam sad. Do you want that?"

Molly looked at their dad with her big brown eyes. She liked their dad, he was kind and gentle. He always gave her food and water and brushed her fur. He also warned her about the dangers on the farm, like the electric fence and the sharp tools. He knew what was best for her. She nodded her head and made a soft noise.

"That's a good girl," their dad said, smiling. "Now, let's go to the pond. I'll come with you and show you the way. And don't worry, I'll bring you a carrot when we come back."

Tom and Sam cheered and thanked their dad. They got back on Molly and followed their dad to the pond. Molly trotted along, feeling curious and excited. She wondered what the pond was like and what frogs looked like. She hoped they would be friendly and not bite her. She was glad she listened to their dad and gave Tom and Sam a chance. She realized that sometimes, it was good to try new things and have fun. She was a happy mule.

Timmy was sad and said, "But mom, I loved that toy. I don't want to be patient and wait for a new one."

His mom hugged him and said, "I know it's hard, but sometimes in life we have to be patient and wait for things. It's important to be kind to others even when we're upset. Let's try to find a way to fix your toy together."

Timmy learned that being patient and kind is important in life, and that using mean words like "hate" can hurt others' feelings.

After they finished their hot chocolate, Timmy said, "Let's go back outside and play!" Lily was happy again. They ran outside and played in the sunflower garden. They whistled and sang songs. It was a fun day!

But then she realized that the necklace belonged to someone else. She felt sad that she took something that wasn't hers. She decided to return the necklace to its rightful owner. 

Lily went back to her mommy and told her what happened. They went on a search to find the owner of the necklace. They asked everyone they saw if they lost a necklace. Finally, they found a lady who was looking for it. Lily returned the necklace and the lady was very happy. Lily felt proud that she did the right thing and learned that it's important to return things that belong to others.

Her mom shrugged and said, "I don't know, maybe it fell down in the wind." 

Lily wanted to help, so she picked up the broken post and tried to fix it. She used some tape to hold it together, but it didn't work. 

Lily's mom said, "It's okay, Lily. Sometimes things break and we can't fix them. Let's go play in the park instead." 

Lily agreed and they went to swing on the swings and slide down the slide. Even though she couldn't fix the post, Lily felt happy because she got to spend time with her mom and have fun.

Jack's friend, Timmy, saw him with the helmet and asked, "Why are you wearing that thing on your head?" Jack replied, "My mom said I have to wear it so I don't get hurt." Timmy said, "I don't wear a helmet and I'm fine."

Later that day, Jack was riding his bike and he got very tired. He saw Timmy riding his bike without a helmet and he wanted to take his off too. But then he remembered what his mom said and decided to keep it on. Suddenly, Jack hit a bump and fell off his bike. His helmet protected his head and he was okay. Timmy saw what happened and said, "Wow, I guess helmets are important. I'm going to wear one too."

But then, the volcano erupted! The boy got scared and tried to run away, but he couldn't. The lava from the volcano covered him and he got hurt. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the park with her mom. They saw a big rock on the ground. "Look, Mommy! A rock!" said Lily. "Can I taste it?" 

"No, Lily. Rocks are not for tasting," said her mom. "They can be very harsh on your teeth."

Lily saw some other kids playing with a ball nearby. She wanted to play too. "Can I play with them?" she asked her mom.

"Sure, Lily. Go ahead," said her mom. "But remember, don't put the ball in your mouth. It's not for tasting either." 

Lily played with the other kids and had lots of fun. She forgot all about the rock and the ball. When it was time to go home, Lily said, "Mommy, I had a great time playing with the kids. Can we come back to the park tomorrow?" 

"Of course, Lily. We can come back anytime you want," said her mom. "But we won't taste any rocks or balls, okay?" 

"Okay, Mommy," said Lily, and they walked home together.

Lily was not sure. She thought the clock was old and modest. She did not want to break it.

"Are you sure?" she asked. "Maybe we should not touch it."

Tom did not listen. He climbed on the clock and grabbed the pendulum. He pushed it hard and made it swing faster.

"Whee!" he shouted. "This is great!"

Lily watched him nervously. She saw the clock shake and creak. She heard a loud snap. The pendulum broke off and flew across the room. Tom fell down with a thud. He hit his head on the floor and started to cry.

Lily ran to him and tried to help him. She saw blood on his forehead. She was scared and sorry.

"Tom, are you okay?" she asked. "I'm sorry, I'm sorry!"

But Tom did not answer. He was still and quiet. Lily did not know what to do. She wished they had never played with the clock. She wished they had been more modest. She wished Tom would wake up. But he did not.

Lila and Ben were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were pirates and explorers. They used a big rug as their ship and sailed to distant lands.

"Look, Ben, there is a treasure island!" Lila said, pointing to the couch. "Let's go and find the gold and jewels!"

They jumped off the rug and ran to the couch. They lifted the cushions and searched for shiny things. They found some coins, a necklace and a ring.

"Wow, we are rich!" Ben said, holding the ring. "This is the best adventure ever!"

But then they heard a loud voice from the kitchen. It was Mom.

"Who cut my rug?" Mom asked, sounding angry. "There is a big hole in the middle of it!"

Lila and Ben looked at each other. They remembered that they had used scissors to make a window in their ship. They had cut the rug without asking.

"Oh no, we are in trouble!" Lila said, dropping the necklace. "What do we do?"

Ben thought for a moment. He had an idea.

"Let's say sorry to Mom and help her fix the rug," he said. "Maybe she will forgive us."

Lila nodded. She agreed with Ben. They took the scissors and the treasure and went to the kitchen. They hoped Mom would not be too mad at them.

"Hey, get out of my truck!" he shouts. He opens the door. He tries to pull Lily and Tom out.

But Lily and Tom are scared. They do not want to get out. They lock the door. They push the horn more. BEEP BEEP BEEP!

The truck driver bangs on the door. He yells at them. He wants them to stop.

But Lily and Tom do not stop. They are happy. They think it is a game. They smile at each other. They push the horn more and more. BEEP BEEP BEEP!

"Let's put some pepper in the soup," Tom said. "It will make it spicy and tasty."

"OK," Lily said. "But not too much. We don't want to make it too hot."

Tom took the pepper shaker and shook it over the pot. He shook it hard and fast. He wanted to make the soup very spicy. But he shook it too hard and the lid came off. Pepper flew everywhere. It went into the pot, on the floor, on the table, and on Tom and Lily.

"Achoo! Achoo! Achoo!" Tom and Lily sneezed. They rubbed their eyes and noses. They felt hot and itchy. They did not like the pepper.

They heard a knock on the door. It was Mom. She came in and saw the mess. She saw the pepper, the pot, the spoons, and the spices. She saw Tom and Lily sneezing and rubbing.

"What happened here?" Mom asked. She was not happy.

Tom and Lily felt bad. They knew they had made a mistake. They wanted to say sorry. But they could not talk. They only sneezed.

"Achoo! Achoo! Achoo!"

Mom sighed. She took a cloth and wiped their faces. She gave them some water to drink. She helped them clean up the kitchen. She was not angry. She was kind.

Tom and Lily stopped sneezing. They felt better. They looked at Mom. They wanted to thank her. They also wanted to be polite.

"Thank you, Mom," Tom said. "We are sorry we made a mess. We were playing chefs. We wanted to make soup. But we put too much pepper. It was not good."

"Yes, thank you, Mom," Lily said. "We are sorry we wasted the pepper. We did not mean to. We were having fun. But we learned our lesson. Pepper is not for playing. It is for eating. But only a little bit."

Mom smiled. She hugged them. She was proud.

"You are welcome, my loves," Mom said. "I am glad you are OK. I am also glad you are polite. You said sorry and thank you. That is very nice. And I am glad you learned something. Pepper is a good spice. But you have to use it carefully. It can make you sneeze and itch. It can also make your food too hot. Next time, you can ask me to help you. I can show you how to make soup. Tom and Lily nodded. They liked the idea. They wanted to make soup with Mom. And they wanted to use pepper. But only a little bit.

Anna felt sad and angry. She thought Tom was mean and selfish. She waited until Tom went inside the house, then she ran to his bike. She climbed on it and tried to pedal. But the bike was too big for her. She lost her balance and fell to the ground. She scraped her knee and cried.

Tom heard her cry and came outside. He saw Anna on the ground and his bike on the grass. He was mad and worried. He shouted, "What did you do? You broke my bike! You shouldn't have touched it!"

Anna looked up at him with tears in her eyes. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom. I just wanted to try it. I didn't mean to break it. Please don't be mad at me."

Tom saw her scraped knee and felt sorry for her. He realized he was too harsh and unkind. He said, "It's okay, Anna. I'm not mad at you. I'm sorry I yelled at you. Come on, let's go inside and get a band-aid for your knee. Maybe later we can play together with your toys."

Anna smiled and hugged him. She said, "Thank you, Tom. You're a good brother. I love you."

They went inside and made up. Anna learned that she should not take things that are not hers without asking. Tom learned that he should share and be nice to his sister. They both learned that trying new things can be fun, but also risky. They decided to be more careful and respectful in the future.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play pretend. They had many costumes and toys in the attic, where they could make up stories and act them out. One day, they decided to perform a show for their mom and dad, who were working downstairs.

Sara wanted to be a princess, and Ben wanted to be a dragon. They put on their dresses and masks and practiced their lines. Sara said, "I am the most beautiful princess in the land, and you are a mean dragon who wants to eat me." Ben said, "I am a hungry dragon who likes to roar and breathe fire, and you are a tasty princess who tries to run away."

They were having fun, until they heard a loud noise from the attic door. It was their little brother, Max, who had climbed up the stairs. He saw Sara and Ben and wanted to join them. He said, "I want to play too! I want to be a knight who saves the princess from the dragon!"

Sara and Ben were not happy. They said, "No, Max, you can't play with us! This is our show, and you are too small and silly. Go away!" Max felt sad and angry. He said, "No, I won't go away! I want to play too! You are mean and selfish!" He ran towards Sara and Ben and tried to grab their costumes and toys.

Sara and Ben shouted, "Stop, Max, stop! You are ruining our show! You are breaking our things!" They pushed and pulled Max, who pushed and pulled back. They made a big mess in the attic, and their mom and dad heard the noise. They came up the stairs and saw Sara, Ben, and Max fighting and crying.

Their mom and dad were not happy. They said, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting and making such a noise? Don't you know this is important work time for us?" They looked at the costumes and toys, and said, "And why are you playing with these old things? They are dirty and dusty and could make you sick. You should play with your new things downstairs."

Sara and Ben felt ashamed and sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom and dad. We wanted to perform a show for you, but Max wanted to play too, and we didn't let him. We were mean and selfish, and we made a big mess." Max felt ashamed and sorry too. He said, "I am sorry, mom and dad. I wanted to play with Sara and Ben, but they didn't want me. I was sad and angry, and I ruined their show."

Their mom and dad felt sorry for them too. They said, "We are sorry, Sara, Ben, and Max. We know you wanted to have fun and show us your talents, but we were too busy and didn't pay attention. We were mean and selfish too, and we didn't appreciate your creativity." They hugged Sara, Ben, and Max, and said, "We love you, and we are proud of you. How about we clean up this mess together, and then we watch your show downstairs?"

Sara, Ben, and Max smiled and nodded. They said, "We love you too, mom and dad. Thank you for watching our show. We will share and play nicely together." They cleaned up the mess, and then they went downstairs. They performed their show, and their mom and dad clapped and cheered. They had a happy and fun time together.

One day, a yellow fox was looking for food in the forest. He saw a big tree with red fruits. He wanted to eat them, but they were too high for him to reach. He thought of a plan.

He found a stick and threw it at the fruits. But the stick missed and hit a bird on the branch. The bird was angry and flew down to the fox.

"Hey, why did you throw that stick at me?" the bird asked.

"Sorry, I did not want to hit you. I wanted to hit the fruits. I am hungry," the fox said.

"Well, you should not throw things at others. It is not nice. And you cannot eat those fruits. They are not good for you. They are sour and bitter," the bird said.

"Really? Then what can I eat?" the fox asked.

"Come with me. I will show you. There are some berries and nuts in the clearing. They are sweet and crunchy," the bird said.

The fox followed the bird to the clearing. He saw many berries and nuts on the ground. He tasted them and liked them. He thanked the bird for helping him.

"You are welcome. I am glad you are not hungry anymore. And I am sorry for being angry. You did not mean to hurt me," the bird said.

The fox and the bird became friends. They shared the berries and nuts and talked for a while. Then they said goodbye and went their own ways. The yellow fox was happy. He had found food and a friend. He did not throw sticks anymore.

One day, they decided to play hide and seek with their costumes. Mia put on a princess dress and a crown. Ben put on a wizard robe and a hat. He also took a magic wand from their toy box. He said, "I will count to ten and then find you. But be careful, my wand can make you disappear!"

Mia giggled and ran to find a hiding spot. She went to the living room and hid behind the sofa. She waited for Ben to come and look for her. She heard him say, "Ready or not, here I come!"

Ben walked around the house, waving his wand and saying, "Abracadabra, where are you?" He checked the kitchen, the bathroom, the bedroom, but he could not find Mia. He went to the living room and saw the sofa. He thought, "Maybe she is behind there."

He pointed his wand at the sofa and said, "Abracadabra, show me Mia!" But nothing happened. He moved closer and looked behind the sofa. He saw Mia's dress and crown, but not Mia. He gasped and said, "Oh no, I made her disappear!"

He dropped his wand and ran to the sofa. He lifted the dress and the crown, hoping to see Mia. But there was only a small mouse, squeaking and nibbling on a piece of cheese. Ben was scared and confused. He said, "Mia, is that you? How did you become a mouse?"

The mouse looked at him and nodded. It squeaked, "It was your wand. It changed me. Please change me back!"

Ben felt sorry and guilty. He said, "I'm sorry, Mia. I didn't mean to do that. I don't know how to change you back. Maybe we can ask Mom or Dad for help."

He picked up the mouse and the wand and ran to find their parents. He hoped they could fix his mistake and bring Mia back. He learned a lesson: never play with magic wands. They can make things disappear.

His mom came to his room. She gave him some water and a hug. She said, "Tom, I know you are sick. But you will get better soon. Then you can play with your friends again. You are a brave boy."

Tom smiled a little. He said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. But I miss my friends. Can I call them?"

His mom nodded. She said, "Of course, you can. They miss you too. They want to hear your voice. They are your normal friends who care about you."

Tom felt a little better. He picked up his phone and called his friends. He said, "Hi, friends. I am sick. But I will be okay. How are you?"

His friends said, "Hi, Tom. We are sorry you are sick. But we are happy you are okay. We are fine. We are playing with the ball. But we miss you. We want you to play with us."

Tom said, "I miss you too. I want to play with you. But I have to rest. Mom says I will get better soon. Then we can play together again. You are my normal friends who make me happy."

His friends said, "We are your normal friends who love you. Get well soon, Tom. We will wait for you."

Tom said, "Thank you, friends. I love you too. Bye."

He hung up the phone and smiled. He felt a little better. He had a normal boy who had normal friends. He wanted to play with them. And he would. Soon.

They saw a big wolf with blue fur and yellow eyes. The wolf was angry and hungry. It growled and showed its sharp teeth. Lily and Ben were scared and wanted to run away.

"Who are you?" the wolf asked. "Why are you in my forest?"

"We are Lily and Ben," Lily said. "We are sorry, we did not know this was your forest. We were just playing."

The wolf did not care. It wanted to eat Lily and Ben. It stepped closer to them and opened its mouth.

"Help!" Lily and Ben shouted. "Someone help us!"

A man with a hat and a gun heard their cries. He was a hunter. He ran to the tree and saw the wolf. He aimed his gun and shot the wolf. The wolf fell down and did not move.

"Lily! Ben! Are you okay?" the man asked. He was their father. He had been looking for them.

"Yes, daddy, we are okay," Lily and Ben said. They hugged their father and thanked him. "You saved us from the blue wolf."

"Let's go home, children," their father said. "The forest is not safe. There are many bad animals here. You should not play here alone."

Lily and Ben nodded. They followed their father and left the forest. They never saw the blue wolf again.

Benny replied, "I want to touch the rainbow, but I don't want to move."

Sammy said, "I can help you. Just pull my tail and I'll pull you towards the rainbow."

Benny pulled Sammy's tail and they both went towards the rainbow. When they reached the rainbow, they saw a pot of gold at the end of it. They both were very happy and thanked each other for helping.

The moral of the story is that if you want something, you have to make an effort to get it. Don't be lazy like Benny, instead, pull up your socks and work hard to achieve your goals.

Crabby was sad and didn't know what to do. Then, a generous seagull saw Crabby's problem and offered to help. The seagull said he would store the shell in his nest until Crabby could figure out a way to fit it in his home.

The eagle thought for a moment and said, "I know just the place! There's a forest at the bottom of the mountain where it's much cooler. Follow me!"

The eagle smiled and said, "I'm happy to help. Remember, sometimes when things get too hot, you just need to find a way to decrease the heat. That way, you'll feel much better." And with that, the eagle flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was so spicy, she made everyone laugh.

One day, Anna asked her daddy, "What is a law?". Her daddy smiled and said, "A law is something that rises above our selfish needs to make us all act in a fair way."

At this, Anna frowned. "That doesn't sound fun at all," she said. But her daddy nodded and said, "It is true. But law is a helpful thing to have. Without it, everyone would do whatever they want, and it wouldn't be fair."

Anna liked the sound of this and nodded thoughtfully. Later that day, Anna saw an old man cross the street when the light was red. She was about to cross herself but then remembered her daddy's words.

So instead of crossing, she waited for the light to change to green. When it did, the old man and Anna both crossed at the same time.

The moral of the story is that it is important to follow the law, no matter how small the law may be. It helps to create fairness and justice for all of us.

So Paul and his mother cooked the cake together. It smelled delicious! But then, suddenly, Paul decided he didn't want to share the cake. He wanted to keep it all for himself.

Paul's mother said, "Paul, that's not nice. You should share the cake with others." But Paul wouldn't listen. He just kept the cake all to himself, and ate it all himself, too.

The end.

The moral of the story is: selfishness leads to bad results. Sharing is caring, and always remember to be generous with what you have.

Lily smiled and agreed to the test. They both rang the bell as loud as they could, but Lily's bell rang the loudest. 

"I wish my bell could ring like yours," Timmy said, feeling a little sad. 

"Don't worry, Timmy. Your bell is special too," Lily said. "It may not ring the loudest, but it has a beautiful sound that makes me happy." 

Timmy smiled and realized that it's not always about being the best, but being unique and special in your own way. From that day on, they both rang their bells happily, knowing that they were both special in their own way.

Sparkle's friends saw her running and asked her what was wrong. Sparkle told them about the dragon and they all started to panic too. They didn't know what to do. Suddenly, Sparkle had an idea. She remembered that she had a special power - she could make things disappear by dancing.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He lived in a place with lots of trees and grass. One day, he saw a little rabbit hopping around. "Hey there, little rabbit," said the lion. "What are you doing in my place?"

"I'm just looking for some food," said the rabbit.

"Well, I'm hungry too," said the lion. "But I don't think you would be very interesting to eat. You're too small."

The rabbit felt sad. He didn't want to be eaten by the lion. So he thought of a plan. He said, "I know a place where there are lots of big, juicy carrots. Would you like to come with me and eat some?"

The lion thought about it. He was very hungry. "Okay," he said. "But if you're lying, I'll roar very loudly."

The rabbit led the lion to a garden full of carrots. The lion was very happy. He ate and ate until he was full. Then, he thanked the rabbit and went back to his own place. From then on, the lion and the rabbit were friends.

They opened the door and climbed inside. They found the keys in the glove box. They put them in the hole and turned them. The car made a loud noise and started to move. Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know how to stop it.

They drove out of the garage and onto the street. They saw other cars and people. They tried to steer and brake, but they did not know how. They bumped into a trash can, a mailbox, and a fence. They made a lot of noise and damage.

A man saw them and ran after them. He was angry and shouted. He wanted them to stop. He caught up with them and opened the door. He pulled them out of the car. He was their neighbor, Mr. Jones.

He was very mad at them. He said they were naughty and dangerous. He said they broke his things and scared his dog. He said he would tell their parents and the police. He said they would be in big trouble.

Tom and Lily were very sorry. They did not mean to cause any harm. They just wanted to play. They cried and said they were sorry. But Mr. Jones did not listen. He was not thoughtful. He was mean. He took them to his house and locked them in a room. He said they would stay there until their parents came. Tom and Lily were very sad and scared. They wished they never saw the old car. They wished they played with their toy cars instead. They learned a hard lesson. The end.

One day, a big truck was driving on the road. The truck had many tires, but one tire was bad. The driver did not know that the tire was bad. He was in a hurry to deliver his load.

The bad tire made a loud noise. It was going to pop soon. The truck passed by a small car. The car had a mom, a dad, and a little girl. The little girl saw the bad tire and felt scared. She told her mom and dad, "Look, that tire is bad. It will pop and hurt us."

The mom and dad looked at the bad tire. They saw that it was very big and very close. They tried to move away, but there was no space. They were trapped. They felt scared too.

The little girl remembered something. She had a toy phone in her backpack. She took it out and pretended to call for help. She said, "Hello, this is the little girl. There is a bad tire on the road. It will pop and hurt us. Please come and save us."

The driver of the truck heard the little girl's voice. He looked at his mirror and saw the toy phone. He realized that the little girl was trying to warn him. He looked at his tires and saw the bad tire. He felt sorry and scared. He slowed down and pulled over. He stopped the truck before the bad tire popped.

The mom and dad and the little girl were safe. They thanked the driver and the little girl. The driver thanked the little girl too. He said, "You are very brave and smart. You saved us all. I will fix my bad tire and be more careful next time."

The little girl smiled and hugged her toy phone. She learned that even a small thing can make a big difference. She learned that it is good to help others and to speak up when there is danger. She learned that she can save the day.

Anna liked to play with her toy animals. She had a lion, a monkey, a giraffe and a bird. She pretended they were in a zoo and she was the zookeeper. She gave them food and water and talked to them.

One day, she found a big cage in the garage. She thought it would be fun to put her bird in the cage and pretend it was a real zoo. She opened the cage and put the bird inside. Then she closed the cage and locked it with a key.

She went to get some seeds for the bird, but when she came back, the cage was empty. The bird was gone. She looked around and saw a hole in the cage. The bird had escaped. She felt sad and scared. Where did the bird go?

She searched for the bird in the garage, in the garden, in the house. She could not find it. She cried and called for the bird. She hoped it would come back.

Then she heard a chirp. She followed the sound and saw the bird on a branch of a tree. It was hidden by the leaves. It looked happy and free. It saw Anna and flew down to her. It landed on her shoulder and nuzzled her cheek. Anna smiled and hugged the bird. She was glad it was safe.

She decided to not put the bird in the cage anymore. She knew it liked to fly and be outside. She made a nest for the bird in a basket and put it near the window. She gave it some seeds and water and said sorry. The bird sang and thanked her. They were friends again.

"Wow, Tim, he is big and strong. Do you think he is friendly?" Mia asks, feeling a little scared.

"Let's find out. Maybe he wants to play with us." Tim says, holding Mia's hand. They walk slowly towards the gorilla.

The gorilla sees them and stops eating. He looks at them with curiosity and tilts his head. He grunts and waves his arms.

"Thank you, gorilla. You are very nice. Can we play with you?" Mia says, taking the banana.

The gorilla nods again and claps his hands. He leads them to a big swing made of vines. He shows them how to swing and jump. Tim and Mia laugh and have fun.

They play with the gorilla until the sun sets. Then they say goodbye and thank him for the banana and the swing. They promise to come back and visit him again. They sail back to their home, happy and tired. They tell their mom and dad about their new friend, the big gorilla.

Anna liked to play chess with her dad. Chess was a game with black and white pieces that moved on a board with squares. Anna had a queen, a king, a horse, a castle, a bishop and some pawns. Her dad had the same pieces, but in a different color. Anna tried to catch her dad's king, and her dad tried to catch her king.

One day, Anna and her dad played chess in the garden. It was spring, and the flowers were blooming. Blooming meant that the flowers opened and showed their colors. Anna liked the yellow flowers, and her dad liked the red ones. They smelled nice and made the garden pretty.

Anna and her dad were having fun, but they were also slow. Slow meant that they took a long time to think and move their pieces. They did not want to make a mistake and lose their king. Sometimes, they stopped playing and looked at the flowers, or the birds, or the clouds.

While they were playing, a bee came to the garden. The bee liked the flowers too, and wanted to get some nectar. Nectar was a sweet juice that the flowers made. The bee flew from flower to flower, buzzing and humming. The bee saw Anna's queen, and thought it was a flower. The queen was white and shiny, and had a crown on her head.

The bee landed on the queen, and tried to get some nectar. But the queen was not a flower, and had no nectar. The queen was a chess piece, and was hard and cold. The bee was confused and angry, and stung the queen. The queen hurt, and fell off the board. Anna saw the bee and the queen, and cried. Her dad saw the bee and the queen, and hugged her. He said it was okay, and that they could get a new queen. He said the bee was sorry, and that it did not know. He said they could still play chess, or do something else. He said he loved her, and that she was his queen. Anna smiled, and said she loved him too. She said they could play chess, or look at the flowers, or watch the clouds. She said the garden was beautiful, and that she was happy.

"What is that?" Ben asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "It looks scary."

They saw some people come out of their cars and run to the hole. They had helmets and suits and tools. They looked like they wanted to see what was in the hole.

"Let's go see, too," Ben said. He grabbed Lily's hand and started to rush to the hole.

"No, Ben, wait!" Lily said. She was afraid. She remembered her wish. She wished that the shooting star would land near their house, so they could see it up close. She did not know it would be so bad.

"Ben, stop!" she cried. "The star is dead. It can hurt us. Please, come back!"

Tom and Jen are twins. They like to play in the park. They see a big rail. The rail is for trains. But there are no trains today. The rail is dead.

"Can we play on the rail?" Tom asks Jen.

"No, we can't. Mom said the rail is dangerous. We can get hurt," Jen says.

"But I want to play on the rail. It looks fun. Please, Jen, let me play on the rail," Tom begs.

Jen thinks for a moment. She loves Tom. She wants him to be happy. But she also wants him to be safe. She has an idea.

"OK, Tom, I will let you play on the rail. But only for a little bit. And only if you hold my hand. And only if you listen to me. And only if you promise to get off the rail when I say so. Do you promise?" Jen says.

Tom nods. He is excited. He promises to do what Jen says. He holds her hand. They walk on the rail. They pretend to be trains. They make choo-choo noises. They have fun.

But then Jen sees something. She sees a big sign. The sign says "Danger. Live Rail. Do Not Touch." Jen is scared. She remembers what Mom said. The rail is not dead. The rail is alive. The rail can hurt them.

"Tom, we have to get off the rail. Now. The rail is not dead. The rail is alive. The rail can hurt us. Come on, Tom, let's go," Jen says.

But Tom does not listen. He is having too much fun. He does not want to get off the rail. He does not see the sign. He does not hear Jen.

"Tom, please, listen to me. We have to get off the rail. Please, Tom, let me help you. Please, Tom, let's go," Jen says.

But Tom does not listen. He does not let Jen help him. He does not let Jen go. He stays on the rail. He makes choo-choo noises. He is happy.

But then he feels something. He feels a shock. He feels a pain. He feels a fear. He screams. He falls. He is silent.

Jen is sad. She is scared. She is sorry. She cries. She runs. She calls for Mom. She wishes she did not let Tom play on the rail. She wishes Tom listened to her. She wishes Tom was alive. She wishes Tom was happy.

The fairy smiled and said, "The sky is blue because of the sunlight reflecting off the clouds. Does that answer your question?"

Jack nodded and thanked the fairy for her answer. Then he continued on his way, talking to the birds and the butterflies as he went.

And they all lived happily ever after.

The neighbour agreed, and after searching all morning, they finally spotted the cows at the edge of a nearby forest. But when they got there, the farmer saw something strange.

The cows were eating something unusual. It looked like meat. The farmer was so mad that he yelled, "What foolishness is this?"

The neighbour said, "I think these cows are lying. I don't think it is meat. Let's take a closer look."

The farmer and the neighbour got closer and closer until they realised what the cows were really eating: leaves from the trees in the forest! The farmer was relieved, and laughed at his foolish cows. But he was also happy that he had a neighbour who was so helpful and could help him out in a tricky situation. The farmer thanked his neighbour and took his cows back home.

She started to cry. She did not know what to do. She wished her mom or dad would come and find her. But they did not know where she was.

Then, she heard a voice. It was a boy. He was unknown to her. He said, "Hey, are you okay? Why are you crying?"

Lily sniffed and said, "I'm lost. I can't find my house. And there is thunder and lightning. I'm scared."

The boy said, "Don't worry. I know where your house is. I live near you. I can help you. Come with me."

Lily was not sure if she should trust the unknown boy. But he seemed nice and friendly. And she was very scared and lonely. So she decided to follow him.

The boy held her hand and led her through the streets. He talked to her and made her feel better. He said, "Thunder and lightning are not so bad. They are just noises and flashes. They can't hurt you. You just have to be brave and manage your fear."

Soon, they reached Lily's house. Lily saw her mom and dad waiting for her. They were happy and relieved to see her. They hugged her and thanked the boy for helping her.

Lily said, "Thank you, too. You are very kind and brave. What is your name?"

The boy said, "My name is Ben. I'm your new neighbor. I just moved in yesterday."

Lily smiled and said, "Nice to meet you, Ben. Do you want to be my friend?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, I do. Do you want to play with me tomorrow?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. But only if there is no thunder and lightning."

They both laughed and agreed.

The moral of the story is: Sometimes, we can find help and friendship in unknown people. We should not judge them by their appearance or fear them. We should also be brave and manage our fears. Thunder and lightning are not so bad, after all.

Sam and Mia felt sorry and scared. They did not know the bird was dangerous. They only wanted to play with it and make it happy. But they made a big mistake. They tried to escape from the bird, but it was too fast and strong. The bird pecked them until they fell down and bled. No one could help them. The bird was wild and mean. Sam and Mia were hurt and sad. They wished they never opened the cage.

At the restaurant, Tom and Lily saw a big cake on a table. It looked yummy. They wanted to have some. But mom and dad said no. They said the cake was for someone else's birthday. Tom and Lily had to wait for their pizza and ice cream.

Tom and Lily were not happy. They did not want to wait. They wanted the cake. They had a plan. When mom and dad were not looking, they got up from their chairs. They sneaked to the table with the cake. They tried to grab a piece.

But they were not careful. They knocked over the cake. It fell on the floor. It made a big mess. Everyone in the restaurant looked at them. They heard a loud scream. It was the birthday girl. She was very sad. She cried.

Mom and dad were very angry. They ran to Tom and Lily. They scolded them. They said they were naughty and rude. They said they had to say sorry to the birthday girl and the restaurant. They said they had to go home. They said they could not have pizza and ice cream.

Tom and Lily were very embarrassed. They felt bad. They said sorry to the birthday girl and the restaurant. But they did not get any cake. They did not get any pizza. They did not get any ice cream. They went home with mom and dad. They had no fun. They wished they had behaved well.

Sara loved to go to the zoo with her mom and dad. She liked to see all the different animals and learn their names. Her favorite animal was the zebra, because it had black and white stripes all over its body. She thought it was amazing.

One day, Sara saw a sign that said "Zebra Talk". She asked her mom what it meant. Her mom said it meant that a zoo person would talk about the zebras and let the kids examine them. Sara was very excited. She wanted to examine a zebra.

She followed her mom and dad to the zebra area, where a zoo person was waiting with a big smile. He said hello to the kids and asked them if they wanted to learn about zebras. Sara nodded her head. The zoo person said that zebras were horses that lived in Africa. He said that they had stripes to confuse the lions that wanted to eat them. He said that each zebra had a different pattern of stripes, like a fingerprint.

Then he said that he had a special surprise for the kids. He said that he had a baby zebra that was born a few weeks ago. He said that the baby zebra was very friendly and curious, and that he would let the kids examine him. He said that they had to be gentle and quiet, and not touch his eyes or ears. He said that the baby zebra's name was Zane.

He led the kids to a small fence, where Zane was waiting. Zane was smaller than the other zebras, and had fuzzy hair. He looked at the kids with big brown eyes. Sara was the first to go inside the fence. She walked slowly towards Zane, and reached out her hand. Zane sniffed her hand, and licked it. Sara giggled. She felt his soft nose, his warm fur, and his smooth stripes. She examined him with wonder. She thought he was amazing.

Sara and Tom were happy. They thanked Mom and Dad. They picked up the shrimps with their fingers and ate them. They said they were yummy. They said they liked shrimps, even if they were fast.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play together. One day, they want to cook something for their moms. They go to the kitchen and find some eggs, cheese, bread and jam.

"Let's make a sandwich with eggs and cheese," Tom says. "It will be yummy."

"OK," Sue says. "But we have to be careful. Cooking is hard. We need a pan, a knife and a spatula."

They get the things they need and put them on the table. Tom cracks an egg and puts it in the pan. Sue cuts some cheese and puts it on the bread. They turn on the stove and wait for the egg to cook.

But they forget to watch the pan. The egg starts to sizzle and smoke. The cheese starts to melt and drip. The bread starts to burn. The kitchen smells bad.

"Oh no!" Tom and Sue say. "We made a mess. Mom will be angry."

They hear a knock on the door. It is their moms. They come back from exercise. They are sweaty and tired. They smell the smoke and see the mess.

"What are you doing?" their moms ask. They are worried and cross.

"We wanted to cook something for you," Tom and Sue say. They are sorry and sad.

Their moms sigh. They are not angry anymore. They are glad that Tom and Sue are not hurt. They hug them and say, "Thank you for trying. But next time, please ask us before you cook. Cooking is not a game. It can be dangerous. And it can make a lot of work."

Tom and Sue nod. They help their moms clean the kitchen. They learn a lesson. They still want to cook, but they will wait until they are older. And they will always listen to their moms.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a picture of an elephant on it. Lila and Tom are curious. They follow the truck.

The truck stops at a big tent. Lila and Tom sneak inside. They see many animals. They see lions, monkeys, horses, and clowns. They also see the elephant. The elephant is gray and has a long nose. He looks sad.

"Hello, elephant," Lila says. "Why are you sad?"

The elephant lifts his nose and makes a loud sound. "I am sad because I am dirty," he says. "I want to bathe, but there is no water here. Only sand and dust."

Lila and Tom feel sorry for the elephant. They look around and see a big bucket. The bucket has some water in it. They drag the bucket to the elephant.

"Here, elephant," Tom says. "You can use this water to bathe. We will help you."

The elephant smiles. He takes some water with his nose and sprays it on his body. Lila and Tom use their hands to rub the water on his skin. They make bubbles and laugh. The elephant feels happy. He is clean and shiny.

"Thank you, Lila and Tom," he says. "You are very kind. You are my friends."

Lila and Tom hug the elephant. They are happy too. They have a new friend.

But then, they hear a loud voice. It is the ringmaster. He is angry. He sees Lila and Tom and the wet elephant.

"Hey, you kids!" he shouts. "What are you doing here? This is not a place for you. Get out of here!"

Lila and Tom are scared. They run away from the tent. They hold hands and look for their parents. The elephant waves his nose and says goodbye.

The end.

At dinner, Timmy's mom made him some soup. Timmy ate it slowly and his stomach didn't hurt anymore. He told his mom about the bird he heard and how it made him happy. Timmy's mom was proud of him for being brave and not foolish.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks, and he always played with his toy vehicles. One day, Timmy's mom gifted him a new toy truck. The truck was big and had many colors on it. Timmy was very happy and thanked his mom.

Later that day, Timmy's friend Jack came to play. Jack saw the new truck and said, "Wow, Timmy, this truck is gifted! Can I play with it?" Timmy said, "Sure, but be careful not to twist it too much." Jack played with the truck and had a lot of fun. Suddenly, he twisted the truck too hard and it broke.

Timmy was sad and said, "Oh no, my truck is broken. What can we do?" Jack replied, "Don't worry, let's ask your dad. He can fix it." Timmy and Jack went to Timmy's dad and showed him the broken truck. Timmy's dad said, "Don't worry, I can fix it." He took the truck and twisted it back into shape. Timmy was happy again and thanked his dad. From that day on, Timmy and Jack played with the truck together and had lots of fun.

She saw her friend Tommy and said, "Hi Tommy! Look, I have a lollipop!" Tommy replied, "Can I have a lick?" But Lily was impatient and said, "No! This is my lollipop! Mine, mine, mine!"

Tommy felt sad but decided to ignore Lily's impatience. They played together and had fun, but Lily kept talking about her lollipop. Finally, Tommy said, "Lily, can we talk about something else? I'm getting bored of hearing about your lollipop."

Lily thought for a moment and realized she was being selfish. She said, "I'm sorry, Tommy. I didn't mean to be impatient. You can have a lick of my lollipop." Tommy smiled and they both enjoyed the sweet treat together. From that day on, Lily learned to share and not be so selfish with her lollipops.

"Who are you?" asked the dragon. 
"I am Jack, the knight," answered Jack. 
"Why are you here?" asked the dragon. 
"I am on a mission to find a treasure," answered Jack.

Jack thought for a moment and then answered, "A banana!"

Max ran and ran until he found a roll of rough paper. He quickly wrapped his ball in the paper and ran out of the lab. The lab owner couldn't see Max anymore because he was hiding behind a tree. Max was relieved to have his ball back and promised to never go into the lab again.

Once upon a time there was a clever fox. He had an urge to find some sausages for dinner. He thought for a while, trying to come up with a clever plan.

He sat under an apple tree in the meadow and thought until something bright came to him. He had an idea! He ran quickly to the farm, dodging all of the animals as he raced.

At the farm, he found the farmer's friendly dog. He watched the dog carefully and then, when the farmer and his wife were not looking, he followed the dog.

The clever fox had an urge to find some sausages. The dog was very intelligent and he knew where they were kept. He followed the dog's lead to a big red barn. The fox spotted a window and saw some big juicy sausages inside. He could not believe his luck!

The fox grabbed the sausages and ran out of the barn and back to his den in the woods. He had a wonderful dinner of sausages that night- all thanks to his clever plan and the intelligent dog.

Sammy felt worried because he didn't win the race. He thought his friends might not want to play with him anymore. So, he decided to practice climbing every day. He practiced and practiced until he finally made it to the top of the tallest pine tree.

Excited to show his friends, Sammy climbed down and ran to find them. But when he got there, he saw that they were all gone. They had left to play somewhere else. Sammy felt sad and alone. He realized that winning wasn't everything and that he had lost something much more important - his friends.

Mommy explained that sometimes things don't grow as we want them to, but that's okay. They can try again and maybe next time the bean will grow big and strong. Lily smiled and hugged her mommy. She knew they could try again and make the bean grow.
