Lily and Ben were twins who liked to swim in the lake near their house. They had a big rubber duck that they took with them every time. One day, they saw a man with a big axe near the lake. He looked grumpy and mean.

"Hello, sir. What are you doing with that axe?" Lily asked.

"None of your business, kid. Go away and leave me alone. I'm going to chop down some trees and make a fire," the man said.

"But why do you need a fire? It's a sunny day and the lake is cool and nice," Ben said.

"Because I'm cold and hungry and I don't like water. Now scram, before I use this axe on you!" the man shouted.

Lily and Ben were scared and ran away. They hid behind a bush and watched the man. He started to chop down a big tree near the lake. He chopped and chopped, but the tree was very strong and did not fall. He got tired and angry and threw his axe on the ground. He sat down and wiped his sweat.

Lily and Ben felt sorry for the man. They whispered to each other and decided to do something nice for him. They took their rubber duck and filled it with water from the lake. They sneaked behind the man and squirted the water on his face.

"Hey, what are you doing? Stop that!" the man yelled.

"Surprise! We brought you some water to cool you down and make you happy," Lily said.

"We also have some sandwiches and cookies that we can share with you. Do you want some?" Ben said.

The man was confused and surprised. He looked at the twins and their rubber duck. He felt a little bit of warmth in his heart. He smiled and said, "Thank you, kids. You are very kind and brave. I'm sorry I was so grumpy and mean to you. I guess I was lonely and sad. Maybe I don't need a fire after all. Maybe I can try to swim with you and your rubber duck."

Lily and Ben were happy and hugged the man. They gave him some food and invited him to swim with them. The man agreed and followed them to the lake. He put his axe away and jumped into the water. He splashed and laughed with the twins and their rubber duck. He felt a lot better and made some new friends.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to others, even if they are grumpy and mean. You never know what they are going through and how you can help them. Sometimes, a little water and a rubber duck can make a big difference.

Tim and Lily were playing catch in the living room. They had a soft ball that they threw to each other. They liked to catch the ball and say "Got it!" or "Missed it!" when they dropped it.

One time, Tim threw the ball too hard and it hit the television. The television made a loud noise and turned off. Tim and Lily were scared. They ran to the couch and hid behind the pillows.

"Uh-oh," Tim said. "We broke the television. Mom will be mad."

"No, no," Lily said. "Maybe it is just sleeping. Maybe we can wake it up."

They peeked from behind the pillows and saw the television. It had a big crack on the screen and some wires were sticking out. It looked rough and hurt.

"Maybe we can fix it," Tim said. "Maybe we can use some tape and glue."

They got off the couch and looked for some tape and glue. They found some in the kitchen and brought them to the living room. They tried to stick the pieces of the television together, but it did not work. The tape and glue did not hold the crack and the wires.

They heard the door open and Mom came in. She saw the mess in the living room and the broken television. She was not happy.

"Tim, Lily, what did you do?" she asked.

Tim and Lily looked at each other and then at Mom. They felt sorry and scared.

"We were playing catch," Tim said.

"And we hit the television," Lily said.

"And we tried to fix it," Tim said.

"But we couldn't," Lily said.

They hung their heads and waited for Mom to say something. Mom sighed and shook her head.

"Playing catch is fun, but not in the living room," she said. "The television is not a toy. It is expensive and fragile. You could have hurt yourselves or started a fire. You are very lucky that nothing worse happened."

She hugged them and said, "I'm glad you are okay, but you have to be more careful and responsible. You have to help me clean up this mess and save some money to buy a new television. Do you understand?"

Tim and Lily nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We're sorry, Mom."

They hugged her back and said, "We love you, Mom."

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They like to run and jump and slide on the grass. They see a big hill and want to go up. They run fast and try to climb the hill.

"Look at me, I am so high!" Tom says to Lily.

"Me too, me too!" Lily says. She tries to catch up with Tom.

But the hill is steep and wet. Tom and Lily slip on the grass and fall down. They roll and roll until they reach the ground. They are not hurt, but they are dirty and wet.

"Oops, that was fun!" Tom says. He laughs and gets up.

"Fun, but silly!" Lily says. She wipes her face and smiles.

They see a man walking his dog. The dog is big and brown and has a collar. The man sees Tom and Lily and stops.

"Hello, kids. Are you OK?" he asks.

"Yes, we are OK. We were playing on the hill and we slipped and fell." Tom says.

"That's too bad. You should be careful on the hill. It can be slippery and dangerous." the man says.

"We know, we know. But we like to play and have fun." Lily says.

The man nods and smiles. He looks at his dog and says, "This is Rex. He is my dog. He is very smart and friendly. Do you want to pet him?"

Tom and Lily love dogs. They nod and say, "Yes, please!"

They go to Rex and pet him. Rex wags his tail and licks their faces. He is soft and warm and gentle.

"Wow, he is so nice!" Tom says.

"He is so smart!" Lily says.

The man is happy. He says, "Thank you, kids. You are very nice and smart too. Rex likes you. Do you want to play with him for a while?"

Tom and Lily are excited. They say, "Yes, yes, yes!"

They play with Rex and the man. They throw a ball and Rex fetches it. They run and chase Rex and he chases them back. They have a lot of fun.

They forget about the hill and the slip and the ground. They only think about Rex and the man and the play. They are happy and grateful. They make new friends.

Lila and Tom were restless. They wanted to play outside, but it was too hot and dry. The sun was bright and made them thirsty. They asked their mom for some water.

"Here you go, sweeties. Drink some water and stay in the shade. It's not good to be in the sun for too long," mom said.

"Thank you, mom. Can we play with the salt?" Lila asked. She liked to make shapes and patterns with the salt on a tray.

"Sure, you can play with the salt. But be careful not to spill it or put it in your mouth. Salt is not for eating, it's for cooking," mom said.

Lila and Tom took the salt and the tray to the porch. They poured some salt on the tray and used their fingers to draw lines and circles. They made a sun, a moon, a star, and a flower. They had fun with the salt.

"Look, mom, we made a sun like the one in the sky!" Tom said.

"That's very nice, Tom. You and Lila are very creative," mom said.

"Can we make a salt cake?" Lila asked.

"A salt cake? How do you make a salt cake?" mom asked.

"We put some salt in a cup and then we turn it over on the tray. Then we have a salt cake!" Lila said.

"Okay, you can try that. But remember, don't eat the salt cake. It's not a real cake, it's just salt," mom said.

Lila and Tom put some salt in a cup and then turned it over on the tray. They made a salt cake. They pretended to blow candles and sing happy birthday.

"Happy birthday, salt cake!" they said.

They looked at the sky and saw that the sun was going down. They realized that they had to go back soon. They also saw that the cloud that looked like a dragon was getting bigger and darker. They heard a loud noise that sounded like thunder.

"Tom, I think the cloud is angry," Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. Maybe it does not want us to go to the mountain," Tom said.

They were scared of the cloud. They decided to turn back and go home. They ran down the path and hoped that the cloud would not follow them.

But as they ran, they saw something that made them stop. A big, shiny, red ball appeared on the mountain. It looked like a giant cherry. It was the most beautiful thing they had ever seen.

"Wow, look at that, Lily!" Tom said.

They did not know that the ball was a trap. It was a magic ball that belonged to the cloud. The cloud was a wicked wizard who liked to catch children and turn them into animals. "Hello, my little snacks. You are very foolish to come to my mountain. Now you will pay the price. I will turn you into mice and eat you for dinner. Ha ha ha!"

Tom and Lily were very sorry that they had not listened to Mom and gone back before dark. They wished they had been honest and not lied to themselves. They wished they had not been greedy and curious. They wished they had never seen the ball.

They hoped that Mom would find them and save them. But they did not know if she could. They did not know if anyone could. They were very afraid and sad. They hugged each other and prayed for a miracle.

Tom takes a stick from the ground and ties a string to it. He makes a hook from a paper clip. He puts a worm on the hook and lowers it into the water. He waits for a fish to bite.

Lily and Tom are having fun. They do not see the sign that says "Do not go near the pond. The water is deep and dangerous."

A big fish sees Tom's worm and swims to it. It bites the hook and pulls the string. Tom feels the tug and gets excited. He pulls the stick and tries to lift the fish.

But the fish is too strong and heavy. It pulls Tom closer to the pond. Tom loses his balance and falls into the water. He screams and splashes.

Lily hears Tom and turns around. She sees him in the pond. She is scared and runs to him. She reaches out her hand and says "Tom, Tom, grab my hand!"

Tom sees Lily and tries to grab her hand. But the water is deep and cold. He cannot swim and he cannot breathe. He feels the fish pulling him down.

Lily and Tom are in trouble. They need help. They hope someone will hear them and save them. They keep calling for help. They keep hoping.

Ben and Sam were brothers who lived on a farm. They liked to help their dad with the animals and the crops. One day, their dad told them he had a surprise for them. He took them to the barn and showed them a big, shiny tractor.

"This is a famous tractor," their dad said. "It belonged to a great farmer who won many prizes. He gave it to me as a gift, and now I want to share it with you. You can take turns to drive it, but you have to be careful and follow the rules."

Ben and Sam were very excited. They wanted to drive the famous tractor right away. Ben went first. He climbed on the seat and started the engine. He drove around the field, feeling very proud. He saw Sam waiting by the barn, and he waved at him.

"Can I have a turn now?" Sam asked.

"Wait a little more," Ben said. "I'm not done yet."

Ben drove for a long time, and Sam got bored. He decided to sit on the tractor's wheel and play with a stick. He did not see that Ben was coming back. Ben did not see him either. He was too busy looking at the sky and the trees.

Crash! The tractor hit Sam and knocked him off the wheel. Sam fell to the ground and cried out in pain. Ben stopped the tractor and ran to him. He saw that Sam had a big cut on his leg and blood on his clothes.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" Ben said. "I didn't see you! Are you okay?"

Sam was not okay. He was hurt and angry. He pushed Ben away and said, "You're mean! You didn't let me have a turn! You're selfish!"

Their dad heard the noise and came to see what happened. He saw Sam's wound and Ben's tears. He took Sam to the house and bandaged his leg. He told Ben to sit on the porch and think about what he did.

Ben felt very bad. He knew he was wrong. He wished he had shared the tractor with Sam. He wished he had paid attention to where he was going. He wished he could say sorry to Sam and make him feel better.

He sat on the porch for a long time, until he saw Sam coming out of the house. Sam walked slowly, with a limp. He looked sad and tired. Ben got up and ran to him. He hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I'm sorry I was mean and selfish. I'm sorry I hurt you. Can you forgive me?"

Sam looked at Ben and saw that he was sincere. He felt his anger melt away. He hugged him back and said, "I forgive you, Ben. I'm sorry I was mad at you. You're my brother, and I love you."

Their dad saw them and smiled. He was glad they made up. He said, "Boys, I'm proud of you. You learned a valuable lesson today. The famous tractor is not as important as your friendship. Sharing and caring are more important than having and keeping. And always watch where you're going, especially when you're driving a big, shiny tractor."

Suddenly, Jane heard a noise. She was so surprised that she almost fell down. It was coming from inside the castle! Jane wanted to see what it was, but Mommy said not to lie. So, Jane stayed away from the castle.

The noise grew louder and Jane saw the castle doors open. Out came a real, pink unicorn! Jane was so amazed that she started to cry. The unicorn rubbed its head against her hand and nuzzled her. Jane was glad that Mommy had made her stay away. The unicorn was real, and the castle was fake.

Mommy told Jane that she was brave for facing the castle and not believing the lie. Jane hugged the unicorn and they both headed back home.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play outside with their dog, Spot. Spot is big and brown and harmless. He likes to chase balls and lick faces.

One day, it is raining a lot. Anna and Ben cannot go outside. They are sad and bored. They look for something to do inside the house.

"Look, Ben," Anna says. "I found a gift under the sofa. It is for Mommy's birthday. It is a big box with a bow."

"Wow, Anna," Ben says. "Can we open it and see what it is?"

"No, Ben," Anna says. "That is not nice. It is a surprise for Mommy. We have to wait until her birthday."

"But I want to see it now," Ben says. He grabs the box and pulls it. The bow comes off and the box opens. Inside, there is a beautiful dress. It is red and shiny and soft.

"Ooh, it is so pretty," Anna says. "Mommy will love it."

"Let me touch it," Ben says. He reaches for the dress. But he is wet from the rain. His hands are wet and dirty. He drops the dress on the floor. It gets wet and dirty too.

"Oh no, Ben," Anna says. "You made the dress wet and dirty. Mommy will be angry. What will we do?"

"Don't worry, Anna," Ben says. "We can dry it. We can use the hair dryer. It will make the dress dry and clean."

Anna and Ben take the dress and the hair dryer to the bathroom. They plug in the hair dryer and turn it on. They hold the dress in front of the hot air. They think they are being smart and helpful.

But they are not. The hair dryer is too hot for the dress. It makes the dress shrink and burn. It makes a hole in the dress. It makes a bad smell.

"Oh no, Ben," Anna says. "You made the dress shrink and burn. You made a hole in the dress. You made a bad smell. Mommy will be very angry. What will we do?"

"I don't know, Anna," Ben says. "Maybe we can hide it. Maybe we can find another gift. Maybe we can say sorry."

But they cannot hide it. They cannot find another gift. They cannot say sorry. Mommy comes home and sees the dress. She sees the hole and the burn and the smell. She is very angry. She is very sad.

"Anna and Ben," Mommy says. "What did you do to my dress? This was a gift from Daddy. He bought it for me for our anniversary. It was very special. It was very expensive. How could you do this?"

Anna and Ben feel very bad. They start to cry. They hug Mommy and say sorry.

"Sorry, Mommy," Anna says. "We wanted to see the gift. We wanted to dry it. We didn't mean to ruin it."

"Sorry, Mommy," Ben says. "We wanted to touch the gift. We wanted to clean it. We didn't mean to harm it."

Mommy sighs. She is still angry. She is still sad. But she loves Anna and Ben. She knows they are young and curious. She knows they are sorry and sad.

"It's okay, Anna and Ben," Mommy says. "I forgive you. But you have to learn to be careful and respectful. You have to learn to not touch things that are not yours. You have to learn to not use things that are not safe. You have to learn to listen and wait. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mommy," Anna and Ben say. "We understand. We will be careful and respectful. We will not touch things that are not ours. We will not use things that are not safe. We will listen and wait."

Mommy hugs Anna and Ben. She kisses them and smiles. She says she loves them. She says they are her best gifts. She says they can still have a happy birthday and a happy anniversary. She says they can still have fun and play. But not with the hair dryer. And not with the dress.

Sam and Tom are brothers. They like to play with their toys in their room. But their mom says they have to organize their toys before they can go outside. She says organize means to put things in the right place.

Sam and Tom look at their toys. They have cars, blocks, dolls, books, and more. They do not know where to start. They feel sad and tired.

"Mom, we do not want to organize. We want to play," Sam says.

"Me too," Tom says.

Mom comes to their room. She sees their toys all over the floor. She smiles and says, "I have an idea. How about we make a game out of it? We can pretend we are sorting cherries. Cherries are small and red and sweet. Some cherries have stems and some do not. We can put the toys that have something long like a stem in one box, and the toys that do not have something long in another box. What do you think?"

Sam and Tom think that sounds fun. They like cherries. They say, "Yes, let's do it!"

Mom helps them find two big boxes. She says, "You can use these stickers to label the boxes. This one says 'stem' and this one says 'no stem'. Can you say that?"

Sam and Tom repeat after mom. They say, "Stem. No stem."

Mom says, "Good. Now let's start sorting. Look at this car. Does it have something long like a stem?"

Sam says, "Yes, it has a wheel. A wheel is long and round."

Mom says, "That's right. So we put the car in the box that says 'stem'. How about this doll? Does it have something long like a stem?"

Tom says, "No, it does not. It has hair. Hair is short and soft."

Mom says, "That's right. So we put the doll in the box that says 'no stem'. How about this book? Does it have something long like a stem?"

Sam and Tom look at the book. They see a picture of a bald man on the cover. A bald man has no hair on his head. They laugh and say, "No, it does not. It has a bald man. A bald man is smooth and shiny."

Mom laughs too. She says, "That's right. So we put the book in the box that says 'no stem'. You are doing great. Let's keep going."

Sam and Tom have fun sorting their toys. They find more things that have something long like a stem, and more things that do not. They use the stickers to label the boxes. They organize their toys in the right place.

Mom is proud of them. She says, "You did a wonderful job. You organized your toys very well. Now you can go outside and play. But first, do you want a cherry?"

Sam and Tom say, "Yes, please!"

Mom gives them each a cherry. They eat the cherry and say, "Yum!"

They hug mom and say, "Thank you!"

They run outside and play. They are happy.

Lily and Max were playing hide and seek in the park. Lily was the seeker and Max was the hider. Max ran behind a big tree and waited for Lily to find him. He was very quiet and still. He enjoyed hiding from Lily.

Lily looked around the park for Max. She could not see him anywhere. She checked behind the swings, under the slide, and in the sandbox. She was getting tired and bored. She did not enjoy seeking for Max.

Then she saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a big mustache that covered his mouth. He was reading a book and did not notice Lily. Lily thought he looked funny and decided to talk to him.

"Hello, mister," she said. "Do you know where Max is? He is my friend and we are playing hide and seek."

The man looked up from his book and smiled. He moved his mustache and said, "Hello, little girl. I don't know where Max is, but maybe he is hiding behind that big tree over there."

Lily looked at the big tree and saw a pair of shoes sticking out from behind it. She recognized them as Max's shoes. She ran to the tree and shouted, "I found you, Max! You are not a good hider!"

Max came out from behind the tree and saw the man on the bench. He recognized him as his dad. He had put on a fake mustache to surprise him. He laughed and said, "Hi, dad! You are a good helper!"

Lily and Max thanked the man for helping them and gave him a hug. The man took off his fake mustache and said, "You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you had fun. But remember, hiding is not always good. Sometimes you need to be honest and show yourself. That's how you make friends and trust people."

Lily and Max nodded and agreed. They learned that hiding can be fun, but only for a game. They enjoyed playing hide and seek, but they also enjoyed being found.

"What is that, Lily?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe it's a star that fell from the sky," Lily said.

"Can we touch it, Lily?" Ben asked.

"I don't know, Ben. Maybe it's hot or dangerous," Lily said.

They looked at the ball of light for a while. Then they heard a voice.

"Hello, little ones. Don't be afraid. I'm a friend," the voice said.

Lily and Ben were surprised. They looked around, but they saw no one.

"Who are you? Where are you?" Lily asked.

"You're the ball of light? How can you talk?" Ben asked.

"I can talk with my mind. I can also hear your thoughts. I'm here to learn about your world and to share some of my knowledge with you," the voice said.

"Wow, that's amazing! Can you show us something?" Lily asked.

"Sure, I can. Watch this," the voice said.

"Yes, I am ready, Tom!" Lila says.

They sit on the sled. Tom holds the rope. Lila holds Tom. They push the sled. The sled zips down the hill. They feel the wind on their faces. They laugh and scream.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom says.

"Look, there is a mule!" Lila says.

She points to a brown animal. The animal has long ears and a fuzzy tail. It is standing by a fence. It is watching them.

"Hello, mule!" Lila says.

The mule does not say anything. It just looks at them. It does not like the noise. It does not like the snow. It is cold and bored.

The sled reaches the bottom of the hill. It stops. Lila and Tom jump off. They run to the mule. They want to pet it.

"Can we touch you, mule?" Lila asks.

The mule shakes its head. It snorts. It kicks the fence. It does not want to be touched. It wants to be left alone.

"Sorry, mule. We did not mean to bother you," Tom says.

Lila and Tom go back to their sled. They decide to leave the mule alone. They go up the hill again. They want to zip down the hill some more. They have a lot of fun in the snow. The mule watches them. It wishes it had a friend.

"Mommy, what is this flower?" she asks, showing her journal.

Mommy looks at the journal and smiles. "That is not a flower, Sara. That is a seed pod. It used to be a flower, but now it is ready to make new flowers."

"Really? How?" Sara asks, curious.

Mommy explains, "Inside the seed pod, there are tiny seeds. If you plant them in the soil and water them, they will grow into new flowers. Do you want to try?"

Sara nods, excited. She and Mommy go to the garden and find a spot to plant the seeds. Sara hopes they will grow into bright and beautiful flowers, not dull and dry ones. She writes in her journal, "Today I learned about seed pods. They are not flowers, but they can make flowers. I planted some seeds. I will water them and watch them grow." She draws a picture of the seed pod and the flowers she hopes to see. She is happy with her journal.

Lily and Tom nodded. They understood. They said, "We will, grandma. We will be quiet and kind. We will watch and listen and learn. We will not splash the animals anymore. We will only splash each other."

Lily and Tom smiled and followed grandma. They were happy. They learned a lesson. They learned to be gentle and respectful with the animals. They learned to splash only each other.

"Okay, that sounds fun," Anna whispered back. She opened the closet and took out some crayons, stickers, and glitter. Ben grabbed some scissors, tape, and paper.

They tiptoed to the cabinet and started to decorate it. They drew colorful pictures on the paper and cut them out. They taped them on the cabinet doors and drawers. They added stickers of animals, stars, and flowers. They sprinkled glitter on the top and sides.

They were so busy and happy that they did not hear Mom coming into the bedroom. She gasped when she saw the cabinet. It was bright and shiny, but also messy and sticky.

"Anna! Ben! What have you done?" Mom asked in a loud voice.

Anna and Ben looked at Mom with big eyes. They knew they were in trouble.

"We decorated the cabinet, Mom," Anna said in a small voice.

"We wanted to make it pretty, Mom," Ben said in a smaller voice.

Mom sighed and shook her head. She was not happy, but she was not angry either. She knew they were just trying to have fun.

"Next time, ask me before you decorate anything, okay?" Mom said in a calm voice. "And help me clean up this mess."

"Okay, Mom," Anna and Ben said in unison. They hugged Mom and said they were sorry. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them.

They cleaned up the cabinet and the floor. They put the crayons, stickers, and glitter back in the closet. They threw away the paper and the tape.

They were quiet, but they were not bored. They learned a lesson, but they also had fun. They decorated the cabinet, but they also decorated their hearts.

Tom and Sue went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and bears. Tom and Sue liked the animals, but they also liked to run and play.

"Can we go to the playground?" Tom asked Mom.

"Yes, but stay close to us. The zoo is very big and busy," Mom said.

Tom and Sue ran to the playground. They saw a slide, a swing, and a sandbox. They also saw a big gate with a lock.

"What is behind the gate?" Sue asked Tom.

"I don't know. Let's find out," Tom said.

He pushed the gate. It was not locked. It opened. Tom and Sue went inside. They saw more animals, but they were not in cages. They were free.

"Wow, look at the zebras, and the giraffes, and the elephants!" Sue said.

Tom and Sue ran to the animals. They wanted to touch them and feed them. But the animals did not like that. They were scared and angry. They made loud noises and chased Tom and Sue.

"Help, help!" Tom and Sue cried.

Mom and Dad heard them. They ran to the gate. They saw Tom and Sue and the animals. They were shocked.

"What are you doing here? This is not the playground. This is the animal reserve. It is not for people. It is for animals only. You could have been hurt. You are very naughty," Mom said.

She grabbed Tom and Sue and took them out of the gate. She locked it. Dad talked to a zookeeper. He said sorry for the trouble. The zookeeper said it was okay. He said the lock was broken. He said he would fix it.

Tom and Sue were very sorry. They said sorry to Mom and Dad. They said sorry to the zookeeper. They said sorry to the animals. They learned their lesson. They never went to the animal reserve again. They stayed in the playground. They had fun, but not crazy fun.

"It's the best toy ever," Tom said.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to go to the park with Mom. The park has swings, slides, and a big pond. Lily and Ben like to watch the ducks in the pond. They also like to watch the vendor who sells ice cream near the pond. He has a big cart with many colors and flavors.

But they also see something different. It is a new flavor that they have never seen before. It is green and has brown spots.

"What is that?" Lily asks the vendor.

Lily and Ben look at each other. They are curious, but also a little scared. They have never tried mint chocolate chip before. What if they don't like it? What if it is too cold or too sweet or too weird?

"Me too," Lily says. She also points to the vanilla.

The vendor gives him a cone with the green ice cream. The boy pays him and thanks him. Then he walks away, licking his ice cream. He looks very happy too.

Lily and Ben watch him. They wonder how the mint chocolate chip tastes. They wonder if they missed something. They wonder if they should have been more brave and tried something different. They wonder if they will ever get another chance.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys in their house. One day, they found a big box in the garage. It had a picture of a robot on it. They opened the box and saw a robot inside. It was shiny and had many buttons.

"Wow, look at this robot!" Tom said. "Let's turn it on and see what it can do."

"OK, but be careful," Sam said. "It looks powerful."

Tom pressed a button on the robot's chest. The robot made a loud noise and its eyes lit up. It stood up and looked around.

"Hello, I am Robo. I am your friend," the robot said.

"Hi, Robo. We are Tom and Sam. We are your friends too," Tom said.

"Can you play with us, Robo?" Sam asked.

"Yes, I can play with you. What do you want to play?" Robo asked.

"Let's play hide and seek," Tom said. "You count to ten and we hide."

"OK, I will count to ten and then I will find you," Robo said.

Tom and Sam ran to hide in different rooms. Robo started to count.

"One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Ready or not, here I come!" Robo said.

Robo walked out of the garage and into the house. He looked for Tom and Sam. He did not see them. He heard a noise in the kitchen. He went to the kitchen and saw a fridge. He thought Tom or Sam was hiding behind the fridge. He pushed the fridge with his strong arms. The fridge fell over and made a big mess. The food and the drinks spilled on the floor.

"Oops, sorry," Robo said. "Are you there, Tom or Sam?"

No one answered. Robo heard another noise in the living room. He went to the living room and saw a sofa. He thought Tom or Sam was hiding under the sofa. He lifted the sofa with his powerful hands. The sofa flew in the air and hit the wall. The wall broke and the sofa fell outside.

"Oops, sorry," Robo said. "Are you there, Tom or Sam?"

No one answered. Robo heard another noise in the bedroom. He went to the bedroom and saw a bed. He thought Tom or Sam was hiding under the bed. He pulled the bed with his mighty fingers. The bed ripped apart and the mattress and the pillows flew everywhere.

"Oops, sorry," Robo said. "Are you there, Tom or Sam?"

No one answered. Robo was sad. He could not find his friends. He did not know he had destroyed the house. He did not know Tom and Sam were hiding in the closet. They were scared of Robo. They did not want to play with him anymore. They wanted him to go away.

"Where are you, Tom and Sam?" Robo asked. "I miss you. I want to play with you. Please come out."

But Tom and Sam did not come out. They stayed in the closet until their mom and dad came home. They saw the house was ruined. They saw Robo was standing in the middle of the mess. They were angry and shocked.

"What have you done, Robo?" mom asked. "You have destroyed our house. You are not our friend. You are a bad robot."

"Please don't be mad at me," Robo said. "I was just playing with Tom and Sam. I did not mean to destroy your house. I am sorry."

But mom and dad did not listen to Robo. They called the police and the firemen. They took Robo away. They threw him in the trash. They never saw him again.

Tom and Sam felt sorry for Robo. They cried for him. They wished they had not played hide and seek with him. They wished they had been nicer to him. They wished they had not lost their friend. But it was too late. Robo was gone. And so was their house. The end.

She said that she loved Lily, but she did not like her behavior.

She played with her toys, but she did not feel happy. She felt lonely and guilty. She realized that she had hurt her mother and her grandma, and that she had been selfish and rude. She said that she did not need any more toys, and that she would share them with her friends. Ben looked and saw the shadow too. He felt a chill in his spine. He grabbed Anna's hand and said, "Let's get out of here!"

Mom heard them and came to the door. She opened it and turned on the light. She saw Anna and Ben, trembling and crying. She hugged them and said, "What's wrong, my darlings? There is no monster in your room. It's just a shadow from the moon."

She showed them the shadow and explained that it was made by a lamp on the dresser. She said, "See? It's not a monster. It's just a lamp. You don't have to be frightened."

Anna and Ben felt silly and ashamed. They realized that they had been too noisy and naughty. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We didn't sleep. We played pirates and ate chocolate. We broke our promise."

Mom smiled and said, "It's OK. I forgive you. But you have to learn to sleep at night. It's good for you. It makes you grow and dream. And you can play pirates and eat chocolate in the morning. How about that?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "OK, mom. We will sleep now. We love you."

Mom said, "I love you too." She tucked them in and kissed them goodnight. She turned off the light and closed the door. Anna and Ben closed their eyes and fell asleep. They dreamed of chocolate and pirates and monsters. But they were not frightened anymore. They were happy.

"Wow, that's a good hiding place!" Lily said, clapping her hands. "Can you find my doll?"

Tim looked around and saw another mound of sand. He started to dig with his hands. He felt something soft and pulled it out. It was Lily's doll, but it was very dirty and wet.

"Oh no, your doll is all messy!" Tim said, feeling sorry.

"That's okay, we can wash her later," Lily said, smiling. "She likes to play in the sand too."

They hugged their toys and laughed. They did not see the giant shadow that fell over them. It was a big dog, who was also playful. He saw the toys and wanted to join the game. He ran towards Tim and Lily, barking happily.

"Hey, what's that?" Tim said, looking up.

"It's a giant!" Lily said, scared.

They dropped their toys and ran away. The dog picked up the toys in his mouth and followed them. He thought they were playing chase. He wagged his tail and ran faster.

"Help, help!" Tim and Lily shouted, running to their mom.

Mom saw the dog and recognized him. He belonged to their neighbor, Mr. Jones. She called his name and he stopped. He dropped the toys and licked her hand.

"Good boy, Rex!" Mom said, petting him. "You scared Tim and Lily, you know. They thought you were a giant."

Rex looked at Tim and Lily with his big brown eyes. He wanted to say sorry, but he only barked. He hoped they would forgive him and play with him again.

Tim and Lily came closer and saw that Rex was not a giant, but a friendly dog. They felt silly for being afraid. They picked up their toys and showed them to Rex. He sniffed them and wagged his tail.

"Can we play with Rex, Mom?" Tim asked.

"Sure, but be gentle with him and your toys," Mom said.

"Okay, Mom," Lily said.

They took Rex to the sand and played with him. They buried and dug up their toys, and threw them for Rex to catch. They had fun and became friends. Rex was not a giant, but a playful dog.

One day, a big dog came to her yard. He saw Lily's bone and wanted it for himself. He barked at Lily and tried to take her bone away. Lily was scared and angry. She growled at the big dog and said, "No! This is my bone! Go away!"

The big dog did not listen. He bit Lily's leg and made her hurt. Lily yelped and dropped her bone. The big dog grabbed it and ran away. Lily was sad and hurt. She limped to her house and looked for her owner.

Her owner saw Lily and hugged her. He said, "Oh, Lily, what happened? You are hurt!" He took her to the vet and gave her medicine. He also bought her a new bone. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry you lost your bone. But I have a surprise for you. Here is a new bone. It is bigger and better than the old one. I hope you like it."

Lily was happy and grateful. She licked her owner and took the new bone. She said, "Thank you, owner. You are very kind. You are my most value thing." She learned that bones are nice, but friends are nicer. She decided to share her new bone with other dogs who were nice to her.

One day, Tom saw a new automobile in the store. It was big and shiny and had lights and sounds. Tom wanted it very much. He asked his mom to buy it for him, but she said no. She said he had enough automobiles and he should share with Sam.

Tom was angry. He did not want to share. He wanted the new automobile. He thought of a plan. He decided to change his old automobile with Sam's new one. He thought Sam would not notice.

He waited until Sam was asleep. Then he sneaked into his room and took his new automobile. He put his old one in its place. He ran back to his room and played with the new automobile. He was happy.

The next morning, Sam woke up and saw his automobile. He knew it was not his. He recognized Tom's old one. He was sad and angry. He ran to Tom's room and saw his new automobile. He shouted at Tom.

"Tom, you are bad! You changed my automobile with yours! You took my new one and gave me your old one! That is not fair! Give it back!"

Tom did not want to give it back. He liked the new automobile. He said to Sam.

"Sam, you are silly! You do not know the difference! They are the same! Go away!"

Sam did not go away. He grabbed the new automobile and tried to pull it from Tom. Tom pulled back and they fought. They broke the new automobile. It did not work anymore. It did not make lights and sounds. It was ruined.

They both cried. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken automobile and the old one. She knew what Tom had done. She was angry and sad. She said to Tom.

"Tom, you are not wise! You are selfish and mean! You changed your automobile with Sam's without asking! You broke his new one and made him unhappy! You should be sorry and say sorry to Sam!"

Tom did not say sorry. He was still angry. He did not care about Sam. He only cared about the new automobile. He said to his mom.

"Mom, you are not fair! You did not buy me the new automobile! You made me share with Sam! I do not want to share! I want the new automobile!"

His mom did not listen to him. She took away both automobiles and gave them to Sam. She said to Tom.

"Tom, you do not deserve any automobile! You need to learn to share and be kind! You will not play with any automobile until you change your attitude and apologize to Sam!"

Tom was left alone in his room. He had no automobile. He had no fun. He had no friend. He was unhappy. He did not change. He did not say sorry. He did not learn. He had a bad ending.

"OK," Tom says. He agrees. He wants to get the berries back too.

They go to the hole. They bend down. They look inside. They see a pair of eyes. They hear a squeak.

"Hello, squirrel," Tom says. He tries to be friendly.

"Go away, humans," the squirrel says. He is scared. He thinks Tom and Sue want to hurt him.

"No, we don't want to hurt you," Sue says. She tries to be nice.

"Then what do you want?" the squirrel asks. He is curious.

"We want our berries," Tom says. He is honest.

"Yes, our berries. The ones you took from our bush," Sue says. She is firm.

"But they are my berries now," the squirrel says. He is greedy.

"No, they are not. They are ours. We planted the bush. We watered the bush. We watched the bush grow. We waited for the berries to be ripe. We deserve the berries," Tom says. He is proud.

"But I was hungry. I needed the berries. I have a family to feed. I have babies in the hole. They need the berries too. They are healthy and good for them," the squirrel says. He is desperate.

Tom and Sue look at each other. They feel sorry for the squirrel. They understand he has a problem. They want to help him.

"Maybe we can share the berries," Sue says. She is kind.

"Share?" the squirrel says. He is surprised.

"Yes, share. You can have some of the berries. We can have some of the berries. We can all be happy," Tom says. He is smart.

"Really?" the squirrel says. He is hopeful.

"Really," Tom and Sue say. They are friendly.

They smile at the squirrel. The squirrel smiles back. He likes Tom and Sue. He thinks they are nice.

They make a deal. They agree to share the berries. They spend some time talking and playing. They become friends. They are happy.

After the bath, Timmy's mommy said, "See, your hands are clean and your hammer is nice and shiny again." Timmy was happy to see that his hammer was clean and thanked his mommy for making him take a bath.

Once upon a time, a little mouse named Timmy was walking in the forest. He saw a big, brown bear with a long tail. Timmy said, "Hello Mr. Bear, why is your tail so long?"

The bear replied, "I use my tail to balance when I stand up on my hind legs. Would you like to hear me sing?"

Timmy nodded his head and the bear began to sing a song about the forest. Timmy loved the song so much that he started to dance. Suddenly, he smelled something spicy.

He asked the bear, "Do you smell that spicy smell too?" The bear said, "Yes, I do. It's coming from the other side of the forest. Let's go and see what it is."

So, Timmy and the bear went to the other side of the forest and found a big pot of spicy soup. They ate the soup and danced together while the bear sang another song. From that day on, Timmy and the bear became the best of friends.

Mittens replied, "I like birds too, but I like to tease them sometimes."

Lily said, "That's not nice, Mittens. We should be kind to all animals."

Tom said, "Do you want to play with it?" The bird said yes and they played together with the stick all day. They had so much fun shouting and playing with the stick that they didn't even notice the sun was setting. 

When it was time to go home, Tom said to the bird, "Thanks for playing with me. Let's play again tomorrow!" The bird nodded and flew away, happy to have a new friend to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy bear named Bobo. Bobo loved to eat cake. One day, he found a small, yummy cake in the forest. He picked it up and started to eat it.

As Bobo was eating the cake, he heard a little girl crying. Her name was Lily. Bobo walked over to her and asked, "Why are you sad, little girl?" Lily looked up and said, "I lost my cake. I am very hungry and sad."

Bobo wanted to comfort Lily, so he gave her the rest of the cake. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, hairy bear! You are very kind." They both sat down and shared the cake. From that day on, Bobo and Lily were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a small village by the sea, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim loved to play near the water when the tide came in. One day, he saw a weak, little fish struggling in the water. Tim wanted to help the fish, so he picked it up and held it gently.

"Hi, little fish!" Tim said. "Why are you so weak? Let me help you." The fish looked at Tim and said, "Thank you, Tim. I got caught in the tide and it made me spin around and around. I'm very tired now."

Tim knew just what to do. He carried the fish to a safe spot in the water, away from the strong tide. The fish started to feel better and thanked Tim. "You're welcome, little fish!" Tim said with a big smile. "Now you can swim and play without spinning in the tide."

The fish swam away, happy and strong once more. Tim felt proud that he could help his new friend. From that day on, Tim and the fish would play together near the water, always watching out for each other. And they lived happily ever after.

Sue felt bad for her brother and stopped making noise. She even brought him a glass of water to help his tummy feel better. From that day on, Tim learned to listen to his mom and not eat too many delicious cookies at once. And Sue learned not to disturb her brother when he needed some quiet time.

Oliver thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's go on an adventure to find a way to make your horn useful." Danny liked the idea and they both went on an adventure.

As they walked through the forest, they found a big box. Danny used his horn to open the box. Inside, they found toys and treats for all the animals in the forest. Danny and Oliver shared the toys and treats with their friends, and everyone was very happy.

From that day on, Danny learned that his horn was useful after all. He could open things and help his friends. Danny was no longer sad and played happily with his friends in the forest.

When mommy and daddy saw the drawings on the walls, they were not happy. They told Lily and Tim that it was not okay to draw on the walls. They said that Lily and Tim needed to be punished. Mommy and daddy made Lily and Tim clean the walls until all the crayon was gone. Lily and Tim were sad, but they learned their lesson. From that day on, they only drew on paper and never on the walls again.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his best friend, a little girl named Amy. They played all day in the sun. The sun was hot, but they did not care. They were happy together.

One day, Amy and Spot were playing near a big tree. Amy said, "Spot, I am hot. Let's sit under the tree and rest." Spot barked and wagged his tail. They sat under the tree and felt the cool shade.

While they rested, a small bird flew down and landed on the tree branch. The bird said, "Hello, my name is Blue. It is hot today, isn't it?" Amy and Spot looked at the bird and smiled. They had made a new friend.

From that day on, Amy, Spot, and Blue played together under the big tree. They were all loyal friends and loved each other very much. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, Tom said to Pinky, "I need to go to town. Can you mind the farm while I am gone?" Pinky nodded her head and said, "Yes, Tom, I will mind the farm." Tom smiled and left for town. 

While Tom was gone, a big storm came. The wind blew hard, and the rain fell fast. Pinky knew she had to mind the farm. She ran to the chickens and helped them get into their warm house. She went to the cows and made sure they were safe too. 

When Tom came back, he saw that the farm was safe. He looked at Pinky and said, "Thank you, Pinky, for minding the farm. You are a very good pig." Pinky smiled, happy that she could help her friend Tom and keep the farm safe.

They have fun throwing earth balls at each other. They laugh and shout. They are very noisy.

But they do not see that they are making a mess. They are throwing earth on the grass, on the flowers, on the bench, and on the people. The people are not happy. They are angry and sad.

"Hey, stop that!" a man says. He has earth on his shirt. "You are ruining the park!"

"Sorry, mister," Tim says. He feels bad.

"Me too," Sam says. He feels bad too.

Their moms come and see what they have done. They are not happy either. They make them say sorry to the people and help clean up the mess.

"Boys, you should not play with the earth like that," Tim's mom says. "The earth is not a toy. It is where we live. We have to take care of it and respect it."

"Yes, mom," Tim says.

"And you should not be so noisy," Sam's mom says. "You should be polite and quiet. You should not bother other people who are enjoying the park."

"Yes, mom," Sam says.

Tim and Sam learn their lesson. They decide to play with their cars and balls instead. They are more careful and quiet. They have fun and make friends with the people. They are happy and so are the people. They love the park and the earth.

"Coal is something you burn to make fire and smoke. Like in the old trains," Sam said.

"Can we burn it and make our trains go faster?" Tim asked.

"Maybe. Let's try," Sam said.

They took the rock and put it in a metal can. Then they found some matches and lit the rock on fire. It made a lot of smoke and sparks. They were excited and ran to get their trains.

She made the worm curl and uncurl like a spring. She smiled and giggled.

"Wow, Lily, your worm can do a trick. That is cool. Can I try?" Tom asked, feeling curious.

"Sure, Tom, you can try. But be gentle. Don't hurt my worm," Lily said, giving her worm to Tom.

Tom took the worm and made it curl and uncurl. He smiled and giggled too.

"Look, Lily, we have a worm spring. It is fun. I like your worm. It is not gross. It is cool," Tom said, giving the worm back to Lily.

Lily and Tom hugged. They were happy. They liked their worm and their stone. They liked each other.

They decided to keep playing in the garden. They saw a drain near the fence. They wondered what was inside.

They walked to the drain and looked down. They saw something furry and brown. It had a long tail and big ears. It was a rat.

"Look, Lily, I see a rat. It is furry and brown. It lives in the drain," Tom said, pointing to the rat.

"Wow, Tom, you see a rat. It is furry and brown. It lives in the drain," Lily repeated, looking at the rat.

They were not scared. They were curious. They wanted to see the rat better.

They leaned over the drain and said hello to the rat. The rat looked at them and squeaked. It was not friendly. It was angry.

It ran out of the drain and bit Tom's finger. Tom screamed and dropped his stone. Lily screamed and dropped her worm. The rat ran away with the stone and the worm.

Lily and Tom cried. They were hurt. They were sad. They lost their stone and their worm. They did not like the rat. It was mean.

They ran to their mom and dad. They told them what happened. Their mom and dad hugged them and kissed them. They put a bandage on Tom's finger and gave him a cookie. They gave Lily a new worm and a flower.

They told them not to play near the drain. They told them to be careful of rats. They told them to be happy with their worm and their stone. They told them they loved them.

Lily and Tom felt better. They thanked their mom and dad. They ate their cookie and their flower. They played with their worm and their stone. They were happy again. They liked their worm and their stone. They liked each other. They did not like the rat. It was mean. The end.

When they reach the top, they see a big field with many flowers and trees. They also see a fence with a sign that says "No entry". Behind the fence, they hear a loud noise. It sounds like a roar.

"What is that?" Tom asks.

"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe it is a lion or a bear."

They are scared and curious. They want to see what is making the noise. They walk to the fence and look through a small hole. They see a big animal with horns and fur. It is a bull. The bull is angry and runs around the field. It sees them and charges at the fence.

"Run!" Tom shouts.

They drop their ball and run back to the hill. The bull hits the fence with its horns. The fence breaks and the bull escapes. It follows them and tries to catch them.

They run as fast as they can. They reach the bottom of the hill and see a man with a hat and a whistle. He is a coach. He is teaching some kids how to play baseball. He sees the bull and the kids.

"Help!" Tom and Mia cry.

The coach blows his whistle and tells the kids to stop playing. He runs to Tom and Mia and picks them up. He carries them to a safe place. He calls the police and the animal control. They come and catch the bull and take it away.

"Are you okay?" the coach asks.

"Yes, thank you," Tom and Mia say.

"Where are your parents?" the coach asks.

"They are at home," Tom and Mia say.

"You should not go to the field. It is dangerous. There is a sign that says 'No entry'. Did you not see it?" the coach asks.

"We saw it, but we wanted to see what was making the noise," Tom and Mia say.

"That was a bad idea. You should always listen to the signs and stay away from the animals. They can hurt you. Do you understand?" the coach asks.

"Yes, we understand," Tom and Mia say.

"Good. Now, where is your ball?" the coach asks.

"We left it on the hill," Tom and Mia say.

"Let's go and get it. Then I will take you home and call your parents. They will be worried about you," the coach says.

He takes them to the hill and finds their ball. It is still red and blue. He gives it to them and they hug it. They are happy to have their ball back. They are also happy to have met the coach. He is nice and brave. He saved them from the bull.

They go home with the coach and tell their parents what happened. Their parents are angry and scared. They scold them for being naughty and careless. They also thank the coach for helping them. They hug Tom and Mia and tell them to be more careful next time.

Tom and Mia say sorry and promise to be more careful. They also say thank you to the coach and invite him to play ball with them sometime. He says yes and smiles. They are friends now.

"OK, but be careful," her dad says. He gives her the lighter.

Mia runs back to Tim with the lighter. She opens the gas tank and puts the lighter inside. She flicks the lighter.

"What did you do?" he yells. "That was a new car! Someone left it here by mistake! You could have been hurt!"

Tim and Mia are sorry. They did not know. They just wanted to play. They hug their dad and say they are sorry. He hugs them back and says he is glad they are OK.

After playing with the dog, Tim and his mom went home. They had a big cake to celebrate his birthday. Tim blew out the candles and made a wish. He wished for more fun days at the park and more dogs to play with.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the beach with his mom. Tim had a mask and wanted to dive in the water. His mom said, "Be careful, Tim. The water is not normal today."

Tim put on his mask and walked into the water. He saw a big fish swim by. "Wow!" he said. "I want to dive and see more fish!"

Tim took a deep breath and dove under the water. He saw many fish and even a crab. Then, he saw something shiny on the bottom. Tim picked it up and swam back to his mom.

"Mom, look what I found!" Tim showed her a shiny key. His mom smiled and said, "Good job, Tim! This key was lost by the beach guard. Now we can give it back to him."

They gave the key to the beach guard, and he was very happy. Tim felt good that he could help, and he learned that even when things are not normal, he could still have fun and do good things.

After a while, Timmy's hands were cold. He realized he lost one of his mittens. His friends helped him look for it. They searched the rough snow but couldn't find it. Timmy was sad but his friends gave him a warm hug to make him feel better. 

From that day on, Timmy made sure to hold onto his mittens tightly so he wouldn't lose them again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a beautiful dress with flowers on it. One day, she went to the park to play. She saw a boy playing with a toy truck. Lily went over to him and said, "Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" The boy said, "My name is Max." Lily said, "Nice to meet you, Max. Do you want to play with me?" Max said, "Yes, I do."

Lily and Max played together for a while. They had so much fun. Then, Lily's mom said it was time to go home. Lily said, "Bye, Max. I had so much fun playing with you. Can we play again tomorrow?" Max said, "Yes, we can." Lily said, "Great! I will introduce you to my other friends tomorrow." 

The next day, Lily went back to the park. She saw Max playing with another boy. Lily went over to them and said, "Hi, Max. Hi, other boy. This is my friend Max. He's my new friend." The other boy said, "I don't want to be friends with him. He's not like us." Max felt sad and went away. Lily tried to make him feel better, but he didn't want to play anymore. Lily said, "I'm sorry, Max. I thought my other friend would like you. I guess not everyone is nice." Max said, "It's okay, Lily. I understand." And so, Lily went home feeling sad that her friend Max didn't have any friends.

Tom brought his friends to see the long tap. They all took turns turning the tap and drinking the water. The long tap supplied water for all the children, and they were very happy. They played and laughed all day, knowing they could always get a drink from the long tap.

Max said, "Tom, I want to play. Please be nice to me." Tom laughed and said, "No, Max. I will not play with you. You are too small and silly." This made Max very sad and angry.

Max wanted to show Tom that he was not small and silly. He made a promise to himself that he would be brave. So, Max went up to Tom and gave him a little bite on the tail. Tom was surprised and scared. He ran away, and Max felt proud of himself for being brave. From that day on, Tom never teased Max again, and they both learned to play nicely together in the park.

Tim and Kim were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They shared their toys and snacks. They were dependable friends.

One day, a big dog came to the park. It was black and brown and had sharp teeth. It barked and ran towards Tim and Kim. They were scared and ran away. But the dog was faster and caught Tim by his leg. It bit him hard and made him bleed. Kim screamed and hoped someone would help.

A man heard Kim and came to the park. He saw the dog and Tim. He shouted at the dog and threw a stick. The dog let go of Tim and ran away. The man picked up Tim and carried him to his car. He said he would take him to the hospital. Kim followed him and cried.

At the hospital, the doctor looked at Tim's leg. He said it was a bad bite and he had to give him a shot. He said the shot would stop the germs from making him sick. He said the dog might have had rabies. He said Tim had to stay in the hospital for a few days. Kim said she was sorry and hugged Tim. Tim said it was not her fault and thanked her for being his friend.

The next day, Kim came to visit Tim. She brought him a balloon and a card. She said she missed him and hoped he would get better soon. But Tim looked pale and weak. He said he felt very bad and his skin was hot. He said the shot did not work and he had rabies. He said he was going to die. Kim was shocked and sad. She did not know what to say. She held his hand and cried.

The moral of the story is: Be careful of strange dogs. They can be dangerous and hurt you. If a dog bites you, you should tell an adult and go to the hospital right away. You should also get a vaccine to prevent rabies. Rabies is a very serious disease that can kill you. You should love and cherish your friends. They can help you and comfort you when you are in trouble.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make different dishes with the pots and pans. One day, they found a big onion in the fridge and decided to use it for their soup.

"Let's cut the onion and put it in the pot," Tim said. He took a knife and tried to slice the onion, but it was too hard and slippery. He pushed harder and harder, but the knife did not move.

"Be careful, Tim! You might hurt yourself!" Jen said. She watched her brother struggle with the onion and felt sorry for him. She had an idea. "Why don't we increase the onion? Maybe it will be easier to cut then."

"How do we increase the onion?" Tim asked. He was curious and tired of the onion.

"We can put it in the microwave. The microwave makes things bigger and hotter, right?" Jen said. She took the onion from Tim and put it in the microwave. She pressed some buttons and turned it on.

The onion started to spin and sizzle in the microwave. Tim and Jen watched with excitement. They hoped the onion would grow and become soft and yummy. But they did not know that onions do not like microwaves. They do not like them at all.

The onion began to smell bad and make noises. It started to crack and pop and squirt juice. Tim and Jen heard a loud bang and saw smoke and fire. The onion had exploded in the microwave and made a big mess.

"Uh-oh," Tim and Jen said. They ran out of the kitchen and looked for their mom. They were scared and sorry. They knew they had done something stupid.

"Mom! Mom! We need help!" they shouted. "We tried to increase the onion and it went boom!"

Their mom heard their cries and came to the kitchen. She saw the broken microwave and the onion bits everywhere. She was angry and worried. She hugged her twins and scolded them.

"What were you thinking? You could have hurt yourselves or started a fire! You should never play with knives or microwaves! You should never increase onions! They are not toys! They are food!" she said.

Tim and Jen felt ashamed and sad. They apologized to their mom and promised to never do it again. They helped her clean the kitchen and threw away the onion. They learned their lesson. They learned that onions are not fun. They learned that increasing onions is stupid.

Lila looked at the shell and said, "I think it is an oyster. Mom and dad told us about oysters. They live in the water and have pearls inside."

Ben's eyes widened. "Pearls? Like the necklace mom has?"

Lila nodded. "Yes, like that. But not all oysters have pearls. Only some. Maybe this one has a pearl. Do you want to open it and see?"

Ben was curious, but he was also scared. He did not know how to open the oyster. He did not want to hurt it or himself. He said, "I don't know. Maybe we should ask mom and dad first."

Lila agreed. She said, "That is a good idea. Let's go and show them the oyster. Maybe they can help us open it. Maybe we are lucky and find a pearl."

They ran to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a blanket. They showed them the oyster and told them what they thought. Mom and dad smiled and said, "Wow, that is a nice oyster. You are very smart to know what it is. And you are very kind to want to ask us before opening it."

They took the oyster and a knife and carefully opened it. Inside, they saw a shiny, white pearl. Lila and Ben gasped. They could not believe it. They had found a pearl!

Mom and dad said, "You are very lucky, Lila and Ben. This is a rare and beautiful pearl. You can keep it as a souvenir of this day. Or you can suggest what to do with it. It is your pearl."

Lila and Ben looked at each other and smiled. They had an idea. They said, "We want to give the pearl to mom. She can make a necklace with it. Then she can have two pearl necklaces. One from dad and one from us."

Mom hugged them and said, "Thank you, Lila and Ben. That is a very sweet and generous suggestion. I love the pearl and I love you. You are the best gifts I ever had."

One day, their mom says, "We are going to visit grandma and grandpa in the countryside. They have a farm with cows, chickens, pigs and a dog. You can help them feed the animals and play outside."

Tom and Mia are very happy and excited. They pack their bags and get in the car. They drive for a long time and see the city change into fields and hills.

When they arrive at the farm, they hug grandma and grandpa and run to see the animals. They pet the dog, feed the cows, collect the eggs and watch the pigs. They laugh and have fun.

But then, they see a big tractor coming. The tractor is loud and scary. It has a big shovel and it starts to dig the ground. Grandma and grandpa look sad and angry. They say, "The tractor is here to build a new road. The road will go through our farm and destroy our land. We don't want the road. We want to keep our farm and our nature."

Tom and Mia feel sad and angry too. They don't want the tractor to ruin their grandma and grandpa's farm. They don't want the road to take away their nature. They want to stop the tractor.

They run to the tractor and shout, "Stop! Stop! Go away! Leave our farm alone! We love our farm and our nature!"

The tractor driver hears them and stops. He gets out and looks at them. He says, "I'm sorry, kids. I'm just doing my job. The road is part of a modern plan to connect the city and the countryside. The road will make it easier for people to travel and trade. The road will bring more money and opportunities."

Tom and Mia don't understand. They say, "But what about the animals? What about the flowers? What about the trees? What about the farm? What about grandma and grandpa? Don't they matter?"

The tractor driver sighs. He says, "They do matter, kids. But sometimes, progress comes with a price. Sometimes, we have to choose between the old and the new, between the past and the future, between nature and modern. It's not easy, but it's how the world works."

Tom and Mia shake their heads. They say, "We don't like this world. We don't like this choice. We don't like this road. We don't like this tractor. We like our farm. We like our nature. We like our grandma and grandpa. We miss our nature. We miss our farm. We miss our grandma and grandpa."

The tractor driver looks at them with pity. He says, "I'm sorry, kids. I wish I could make you happy. But I can't. I have to do my job. I have to build this road. I have to be modern."

He gets back in the tractor and starts the engine. He says, "Goodbye, kids. Goodbye, farm. Goodbye, nature."

He drives away, leaving behind a trail of dust and tears.

She reached for a fork, but it was very hot. She burned her hand and cried out loud. Mommy heard her and ran to the kitchen. She saw Lily holding her hand and the dishwasher door open. She recognized the fork that Lily had dropped on the floor. She was angry and scared.

"Lily, what did you do? I told you not to touch the dishwasher! You could have hurt yourself badly! How many times do I have to tell you to listen to me?" Mommy shouted.

Lily was confused. "Why? Where are you going?"

Lily was a clever girl who liked to play pretend. She had a big mirror in her room, where she could see herself and make funny faces. One day, she decided to be a lion, and put on a yellow dress and a brown scarf around her neck. She looked at herself in the mirror and smiled.

"Roar!" she said, pretending to be fierce. "I am the king of the jungle!"

She ran around her room, jumping on her bed and growling. She had so much fun, she did not hear her mom calling her for lunch.

"Lily, come downstairs, please!" her mom said. "It's time to eat!"

Lily did not answer. She was too busy being a lion.

Her mom came upstairs and knocked on her door. She opened it and saw Lily in her lion costume, still roaring at the mirror.

"What are you doing, sweetie?" her mom asked.

"I am a lion, mom!" Lily said proudly. "Can't you see?"

Her mom smiled and hugged her. "You are a very clever lion, Lily. But even lions need to eat, you know. Come on, let's go have some soup and bread."

Lily nodded and took off her scarf. She followed her mom downstairs, but not before giving one last roar at the mirror. She liked being a lion, but she also liked being a girl. And she loved her mom very much.

Lila wanted to bring her old doll to the park. She loved her doll very much. She gave her doll a name, a dress and a hat. She talked to her doll every day.

But her mom said no. She said the doll was too old and dirty. She said the doll might get lost or broken at the park. She said Lila should bring a new toy instead.

Lila was sad and angry. She did not want a new toy. She wanted her old doll. She said to her mom, "Please, please, please, let me bring my doll. She is my best friend. She wants to see the park too."

Her mom was persistent. She said no again and again. She said Lila had to listen to her. She said she knew what was best for Lila and her doll.

Lila did not give up. She was persistent too. She hid her doll in her backpack. She hoped her mom would not see it. She wanted to surprise her doll with the park. She thought her doll would be happy.

Tom and Lily were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. They had many blocks of different colors and shapes.

"Look, Lily, I made a big tower!" Tom said, showing his creation. "It is taller than you!"

Lily smiled and clapped her hands. "Wow, Tom, that is a great tower! Can I join you and make one too?"

"Sure, Lily, you can join me. Here, take some blocks and build next to me." Tom said, sharing his blocks with his sister.

They were having fun, building and talking, when they heard a loud noise from outside. It sounded like a big truck or a plane. They ran to the window and looked out.

They saw a big machine with a long hose and a big fan. It was blowing dust and leaves and trash from the street. The dust was flying everywhere and making the air dirty.

"Wow, what is that?" Lily asked, curious.

"That is a sweeper. It cleans the street. But it is very loud and dusty." Tom explained.

"I don't like it. It hurts my ears and makes me sneeze." Lily said, covering her nose.

"Me neither. Let's go back to our blocks. They are more fun and quiet." Tom said, pulling Lily away from the window.

They went back to their blocks and continued to play. They forgot about the sweeper and the dust. They were happy to join each other and make beautiful things.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big box of bones. They can make animals and people with the bones. They can also make scary things, like monsters and ghosts.

One day, they find a new bone in the box. It is a skull. It has two holes for eyes and a hole for a mouth. It looks very fancy and shiny. Anna and Ben both want the skull for their game.

"I saw it first!" Anna says. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Ben says. "I want it more!"

They pull the skull from each other. They are angry and loud. They do not want to share.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the skull and is surprised. She knows it is not a toy. It is a real skull. It belongs to Dad. He is a doctor and he uses it to learn about the head.

"Anna, Ben, stop!" Mom says. "This is not a toy. This is Dad's skull. He needs it for his work. You cannot play with it. It is not safe."

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They did not know it was Dad's skull. They let go of the skull and give it to Mom. They say sorry to Mom and to each other.

Mom smiles and hugs them. She says it is okay. She says they can play with the other bones, but not the skull. She says she will find them a new toy, something more fun and less fancy. She says she loves them.

Anna and Ben are happy. They say they love Mom too. They go back to their game. They make a big dinosaur with the bones. They have fun and forget about the skull.

Lily liked to watch the birds in the sky. She saw many kinds of birds, but her favorite was the dove. The dove was white and soft and made a gentle sound. Lily wanted to touch the dove and be its friend.

One day, Lily saw a dove sitting on a branch near her window. She ran to get some bread and opened the window. She threw some bread crumbs to the dove and said, "Hello, dove. I like you. Do you want to be my friend?"

The dove looked at Lily and tilted its head. It flew closer to the window and pecked at the bread. It cooed softly and nodded. Lily smiled and reached out her hand. The dove hopped on her finger and let her stroke its feathers.

Lily was very happy. She said, "You are so nice, dove. I believe you are a magic dove. Can you grant me a wish?"

The dove blinked and nodded again. It whispered in Lily's ear, "I can grant you one wish, but you have to be careful what you wish for. Some wishes are not good for you."

Lily thought for a moment. She said, "I wish I could fly like you, dove. I want to see the world and be free."

The dove sighed and said, "Are you sure, Lily? Flying is not easy. There are many dangers and troubles in the sky. You might miss your home and your family. You might get lost or hurt."

Lily nodded. She said, "I am sure, dove. I want to fly. Please, grant me my wish."

The dove said, "Very well, Lily. I will grant you your wish. But remember, you can only fly for one day. When the sun sets, you will turn back into a girl. And you have to come back to this window, or you will be stuck as a bird forever."

Lily agreed. She said, "Thank you, dove. I will come back, I promise."

The dove touched Lily's nose with its beak and said, "Close your eyes, Lily. And make your wish."

Lily closed her eyes and wished with all her heart. She felt a strange sensation in her body. She felt her arms become wings, her legs become claws, her hair become feathers. She opened her eyes and saw that she had turned into a dove. A pale dove, like the one on her finger.

She gasped and said, "Wow, dove. You did it. You made me a dove."

The dove smiled and said, "Yes, Lily. I did. Now, let's fly. But don't forget your promise."

Lily nodded and said, "I won't, dove. Let's fly."

They flew out of the window and into the sky. They soared and glided and circled and dived. They saw many things and had many adventures. Lily was happy and free. She felt like she was living a dream.

But she did not know that the dove had a secret. A secret that would change everything. A secret that would make her wish come true in a way she did not expect. A secret that would make her regret her wish. A secret that would make her cry. A secret that would make her pale.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. Sara had a box full of dolls and Tom had a box full of cars. They liked to share their toys and make stories with them.

One day, Sara found a new doll in her box. It was very pretty, with long hair and a shiny dress. She showed it to Tom and said, "Look, Tom, I have a new doll. She is so nice. Do you want to play with her?"

Tom looked at the doll and saw something strange. He took the doll from Sara and pulled her hair. The hair came off and he saw a plastic head. He said, "Sara, this is not a real doll. This is a fake doll. Someone put hair on a plastic head. Look, it can snap off."

He snapped off the plastic head and showed it to Sara. Sara was very sad and angry. She said, "Tom, you are mean. You broke my new doll. Give it back to me. It is not fake, it is special."

She tried to grab the doll from Tom, but he held it tight. They started to fight and pull the doll. The doll broke into more pieces and fell on the floor. Sara and Tom both cried and shouted.

Their mom heard the noise and came to the living room. She saw the broken doll and the upset children. She said, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting? What happened to this doll?"

Sara and Tom both tried to explain, but they talked at the same time. Their mom could not understand them. She said, "Stop, stop, stop. I don't want to hear any more. You both need to calm down and say sorry to each other. This doll was a gift from your aunt. She made it for you with love. It was not fake, it was unique. But you did not take care of it and you ruined it. Now you have no doll and no car. You have to learn to respect your toys and your siblings."

She took the broken doll and the box of cars and put them away. She said, "You can have your toys back when you show me that you can play nicely and share. Now go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Sara and Tom felt very sorry and ashamed. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They went to their rooms and thought about how to be better friends. They decided to make a new doll and a new car for each other with paper and crayons. They hoped their mom and their aunt would forgive them and be proud of them.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw some fireworks in a box near their house. They were curious and wanted to see them. They took the box and ran to the park.

"Let's make them go high in the sky!" Tom said.

"But how?" Lily asked.

"Maybe we need a match," Tom said. He found one in his pocket and lit it.

"Be careful, Tom!" Lily said. "That could be dangerous!"

But Tom did not listen. He threw the match into the box and waited for the fireworks to happen. But nothing happened. He went closer to the box and looked inside.

Suddenly, there was a loud bang and a bright flash. The fireworks exploded in Tom's face. He screamed and fell to the ground. Lily ran to him and saw that he was hurt. His eyes were red and his skin was burned. She cried and called for help.

Soon, their parents and a doctor came. They took Tom to the hospital and treated his wounds. Lily stayed with him and hugged him. She was sorry for what happened.

"I'm sorry, Tom," she said. "I should have stopped you."

"I'm sorry, too, Lily," Tom said. "I should have listened to you. I was foolish and reckless. I learned my lesson. Fireworks are not toys. They are dangerous and can hurt us. We should never play with them."

Lily nodded and kissed his cheek. They both learned a valuable lesson that day. They promised to be more careful and respectful of fireworks. They also thanked their parents and the doctor for helping them. They hoped that Tom would heal soon and that they could play outside again. But they would never touch fireworks again.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big bunch of grapes on a bench. They are hungry and want to eat them.

But then, a big dog comes to the bench. It sees the grapes and barks. It wants to eat them too.

The dog does not listen. It jumps on the bench and tries to grab the grapes.

Ben and Mia are scared. They run away from the dog.

They see a man coming to the park. He has a leash in his hand. He is the dog's owner.

"Hey, stop! That's my dog!" the man yells.

He runs to the bench and catches the dog. He puts the leash on the dog and says sorry to Ben and Mia.

"I'm sorry, kids. He is a good dog, but he does not understand that grapes are not for him. They can make him sick. He is too powerful for his own good," the man says.

Ben and Mia nod. They understand. They are not mad at the dog. They are glad he is not sick.

They go back to the bench and get their grapes. They share them with the man and the dog.

They all eat some grapes and feel happy. They make new friends.

"No, Anna. We can't let the dog go. The dog is part of the lab. The lab is important. You have to understand," her dad says.

Anna does not understand. She feels angry and sad. She thinks her dad is not nice. She thinks the lab is not nice. She thinks the dog is very nice. She wants to be friends with the dog.

"I have an idea," he says. "We can use our hands to talk to him. My mom says that is how some people talk to deaf people. She says it is called sign language. She can teach us some words."

Lily likes the idea. She thinks it is very smart.
