Lily and Ben were friends who liked to ride bikes. Lily had a red bike with a bell and a basket. Ben had a blue bike with a horn and a flag. They rode their bikes to the park every day.

One day, they saw a new bike in the park. It was big and shiny and had many pedals. Lily and Ben wanted to try it. They went closer and saw a sign that said "Do not touch".

"Who owns this bike?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, but it looks fun," Ben said.

"Let's ride it," Lily said. She was bossy and did not like rules.

"No, we can't. The sign says no," Ben said. He was careful and did not want trouble.

Lily did not listen to Ben. She climbed on the bike and pushed a pedal. The bike made a loud noise and started to move. Lily was scared and screamed.

"Help me, Ben!" she cried.

Ben ran after her and tried to catch her. The bike was too fast and too big. It bumped into a tree and fell over. Lily and Ben fell off and got hurt.

They heard a voice behind them. It was angry and loud.

"Who are you and what are you doing with my bike?" the voice asked.

It was the owner of the bike. He was a big man with a beard and a hat. He looked at Lily and Ben with a frown.

Lily and Ben were sorry and scared. They did not know what to say. They learned a lesson that day. They should not touch things that are not theirs. They should listen to signs and to Ben. They should not be bossy and question everything. They should be nice and respectful.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make a club for car lovers. They call it the Speed Club.

One day, they go to the park with their cars. They find a big hill. They want to see whose car can go faster down the hill. They put their cars at the top of the hill and say "Ready, set, go!"

The cars start to roll down the hill. They go very fast. Sam and Ben run after them. They cheer for their cars. "Go, go, go!" they shout.

But then, something happens. One of the cars hits a rock and flies off the hill. It lands in a distant pond. It is Sam's car. Sam is sad. He likes his car very much. He does not want to lose it.

Ben sees Sam's car in the pond. He feels sorry for Sam. He says "Don't worry, Sam. I will help you get your car back. We are friends. We are in the Speed Club." He takes off his shoes and socks and jumps into the pond. He swims to the car and grabs it. He brings it back to Sam.

Sam is happy. He hugs Ben and says "Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend. You are the best in the Speed Club." They dry the car with a towel and play with it again. They have fun. They are happy. They are the Speed Club.

Lily liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a pink doll. She named her doll Rose and gave her hugs and kisses. She also liked to talk to her doll and tell her stories.

One day, Lily's big brother Tom came into her room. He was angry because Lily had taken his ball. He saw Lily and Rose on the bed. He wanted to make Lily sad. He grabbed Rose and threw her on the floor. He stepped on her and ripped her dress. He destroyed Lily's doll.

Lily saw what Tom did and started to cry. She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Mom was very mad at Tom. She told him to say sorry to Lily and give her a new doll. She also told him that he had no wisdom. Wisdom is when you know what is good and what is bad. Wisdom is when you are kind and gentle, not mean and rough.

Tom felt sorry for what he did. He realized he was wrong and he hurt Lily's feelings. He said sorry to Lily and gave her a new doll. He also gave her his ball and said they could share. Lily forgave Tom and hugged him. She thanked him for the new doll and the ball. She also gave him a kiss on the cheek.

Lily and Tom learned a lesson that day. They learned to respect each other's toys and feelings. They learned to be nice and not destroy things. They learned to have wisdom and love.

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play outside, but it was too cold. They looked around the house for something fun to do.

"Let's make a snowman!" Lily said. She had an idea. She ran to the kitchen and opened the freezer. She took out a big bag of ice cubes.

"Look, Ben, we can use these to make a snowman!" she said. She dumped the ice cubes on the floor and started to stack them.

Ben was not sure. He thought the ice cubes were too small and slippery to make a good snowman. He said, "Lily, I don't think this will work. The ice cubes will melt and make a mess. And they are cold and hard. They are not like snow."

Lily did not listen. She said, "No, Ben, this will be a great snowman. We just need to improve it. We can use a carrot for the nose, and buttons for the eyes, and a scarf for the neck. Come on, help me!"

Ben sighed. He did not want to hurt Lily's feelings. He said, "Okay, Lily, I will help you. But I don't think this will be a fine snowman."

They worked together to make the ice cube snowman. They used a carrot, buttons, a scarf, and a hat. They stepped back and looked at their creation.

Lily was proud. She said, "See, Ben, this is a fine snowman. He is smiling and happy. He is our friend."

Ben was not impressed. He said, "Lily, this is not a fine snowman. He is small and lumpy. He is dripping and wet. He is not our friend. He is a freezer monster."

Lily and Ben heard a loud noise. They turned around and saw their mom. She was angry. She said, "What are you doing? Why did you take out all the ice cubes from the freezer? Why did you make this mess on the floor? This is not a snowman. This is a disaster."

Lily and Ben were scared. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were bored. We wanted to make a snowman. We tried to improve it. We thought it was fine."

Mom shook her head. She said, "No, Lily and Ben, this is not fine. This is a waste of ice cubes. And a waste of time. And a waste of food. And a waste of energy. You need to clean up this mess. And then you need to go to your room. And think about what you did."

Lily and Ben felt bad. They said, "Yes, mom. We are sorry. We will clean up. And we will go to our room. And we will think about what we did."

They cleaned up the mess. They threw away the ice cubes. They put back the carrot, the buttons, the scarf, and the hat. They wiped the floor. They said goodbye to the ice cube snowman. They did not think he was fine anymore. They thought he was a freezer monster.

They went to their room. They sat on their bed. They were quiet. They thought about what they did. They did not want to make mom angry again. They did not want to make a freezer monster again. They wanted to make a real snowman. They hoped it would snow soon. They hoped they could improve their snowman skills. They hoped mom would forgive them. They hoped they could play outside soon. They hoped everything would be fine.

Tom and Anna love to watch shows at the theater. They like to see people sing and dance and tell stories on the big stage. Sometimes they clap and laugh and sometimes they feel sad or scared. But they always have fun.

One day, they go to the theater with their mom and dad. They have tickets for a jolly show about a silly monkey and his friends. They are very excited. They find their seats and wait for the show to start.

But before the show can start, a loud voice says: "Sorry, everyone. The show is canceled. The monkey is sick and cannot perform. Please come back another day."

Tom and Anna are very disappointed. They want to see the monkey and his friends. They start to cry and whine. They say: "This is not fair. We want to see the show. We don't want to go home."

Their mom and dad try to calm them down. They say: "We know you are sad, but you have to be patient and understanding. The monkey is sick and he needs to rest. He cannot make you happy if he is not happy himself. Maybe we can see the show another day, or watch something else instead."

Tom and Anna think about what their mom and dad say. They realize that they are being selfish and rude. They say: "We are sorry, mom and dad. We are sorry, monkey and friends. We hope you get well soon. We will come back another day and be more polite."

They wipe their tears and smile. They hold their mom and dad's hands and leave the theater. They see other people who are also sad, but they try to cheer them up. They say: "Don't be sad. The show will be back soon. The monkey is jolly and he will make you laugh again."

The moral of the story is: Be patient and understanding when things don't go your way. Don't be selfish and rude. Think about how others feel and try to make them happy.

Anna grabbed the stick and waved it around in the air for a few seconds. Then she carefully used it to pick up the ice and throw it away. She was so thrilled when she saw the success of her throw! 

Bob and Anna had lots of fun playing their ice game the whole day. And they never forgot how Bob helped Anna mark the ice.

Amy had an idea. She told the lion, "Let's play a game. When you want to roar, just laugh instead." The lion tried it, and everyone in the castle was happy. They did not cry anymore when they heard the lion. The lion and Amy became best friends, and they lived happily in the castle together.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a compassionate wolf. This wolf was not like other wolves. He was kind and gentle, and he loved to help his friends. He always shared his food and played nice games with them.

One day, the wolf found a small toy on the ground. The toy did not belong to him, but he wanted to find out who it belonged to. So, he asked all his friends, like the squirrel, the rabbit, and the deer, but none of them knew who the toy belonged to.

Finally, the compassionate wolf met a little girl who was crying. She had lost her toy and could not find it. The wolf showed her the toy he found, and the little girl was very happy. The toy belonged to her. She thanked the wolf, and they became good friends. From that day on, they played together in the forest and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird named Bobo. Bobo loved to soar high in the sky. One day, Bobo saw a log on the ground. The log was tight between two rocks. Bobo wanted to help the log.

Bobo flew down and tried to push the log. He pushed and pushed, but the log was too tight. Bobo did not give up. He called his friends, the ants, to help him. The ants came and helped Bobo push the log. Together, they pushed and pushed, and the log was free!

The log was happy and thanked Bobo and the ants. Bobo learned that when we work together, we can do big things. And that was the moral of the story: always help your friends and work together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim lived in a big building with his mom and dad. One day, Tim wanted to go outside to play. He had to use the elevator to go down.

Tim walked to the elevator and pushed the button. The doors opened, and he entered. Tim pushed the button with the number 1 on it. But the elevator went up instead of down! Tim felt upset because he wanted to go down to play.

The elevator stopped, and the doors opened. Tim saw a kind old lady. She knew Tim was upset and helped him. She pushed the right button, and the elevator went down. Tim was happy now. He thanked the old lady and went outside to play.

Once upon a time, there was a popular pilot. He flew a big plane in the sky. All the kids loved to see him fly high.

One day, the pilot quit his job. He wanted to play with the kids more. The kids were sad, but they were also happy to play with him.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Ben had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were having fun, but Ben wanted to see Lily's doll.

"Can I play with your doll?" Ben asked.

"No, it's mine. You have your truck," Lily said.

Ben did not like that. He wanted to play with both toys. He tried to grab the doll from Lily, but she held it tight. Ben got angry and pinched Lily's arm.

"Ow! That hurts!" Lily cried. She let go of the doll and rubbed her arm.

Ben took the doll and smiled. He looked at the doll's dress. It had a zipper on the back. Ben pulled the zipper down and up, down and up. He liked the sound it made.

Lily was still crying. She ran to their mom, who was in the kitchen. She showed her the red mark on her arm.

"Mom, Ben pinched me! He took my doll and played with the zipper!" Lily sobbed.

Mom frowned. She took Lily in her arms and kissed her arm.

"I'm sorry, Lily. That was not nice of Ben. Are you okay?" Mom asked.

"I'm fine, Mom. But I want my doll back," Lily said.

Mom nodded. She carried Lily to the living room, where Ben was still playing with the doll. She took the doll from Ben and gave it to Lily.

"Ben, you need to say sorry to Lily. You hurt her and you took her toy. That was wrong," Mom said.

Ben looked down. He knew he did something bad. He felt sorry for Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I won't pinch you or take your doll again," Ben said.

Lily smiled. She hugged her doll and then hugged Ben.

"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. Do you want to play with my doll together?" Lily asked.

Ben nodded. He smiled too. He hugged Lily back.

"Thank you, Lily. You are a good sister. Can I play with the zipper?" Ben asked.

Lily giggled. She nodded.

"Sure, Ben. You can play with the zipper. But be gentle," Lily said.

Mom smiled. She was glad they made up. She watched them play with the doll and the truck. They were happy.

Lily loved to read books. She had many books in her room. She liked to read them with her mom or dad. Sometimes she read them by herself.

One day, Lily wanted to read a new book. She saw it on the shelf. It had a picture of a princess and a dragon. She took the book and went to her bed. She opened the book and started to read.

But the book was hard. It had many big words that Lily did not know. She tried to sound them out, but she could not. She felt upset. She wanted to read the book, but she could not.

She called her mom. "Mom, can you help me read this book?" she asked.

Mom came to her room. She saw the book. She smiled. "This book is for older kids, Lily. It is too hard for you right now. Why don't you pick another book that you can read?"

Lily did not like that. She wanted to read the book. She did not want to pick another book. She said, "No, I want to read this book. I can read it. You don't help me."

Mom felt sad. She did not want to make Lily angry. She said, "Lily, I am sorry. I am not trying to be mean. I am trying to help you. Reading is fun, but it can also be hard. You need to learn new words and new sounds. You can read this book when you are older. But for now, let's find a book that you can enjoy and understand."

Lily thought about it. She looked at the book. She looked at her mom. She knew her mom loved her. She knew her mom wanted her to be happy. She said, "Okay, mom. I am sorry. I was upset. Can you help me find another book?"

Mom hugged her. She said, "Of course, Lily. I love you. Let's go to the shelf and see what we can find."

They went to the shelf. They found a book that Lily liked. It had a picture of a cat and a mouse. It had simple words that Lily could read. They went back to the bed. They read the book together. They had fun. Lily was happy. She loved to read books.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with many acorns on the ground. Lily picked up an acorn and said, "Look, Ben, this is an acorn. It is from the tree. It is brown and hard."

Ben took the acorn and said, "Can I eat it? Is it tasty?"

Lily shook her head and said, "No, Ben, you cannot eat it. It is not tasty. It is for the squirrels. They like acorns. They store them for winter."

Ben nodded and said, "Oh, I see. Then let's play with them. Let's see who can balance more acorns on their head."

Lily and Ben laughed and started to balance acorns on their heads. They tried to walk and not drop them. They had fun and counted how many acorns they could balance. Lily balanced four acorns and Ben balanced three. They were proud of themselves.

Then they saw a squirrel watching them from the tree. The squirrel looked hungry and curious. It jumped down and ran towards them. It grabbed an acorn from Ben's head and ran away. Ben and Lily were surprised and said, "Hey, that's our acorn!"

The squirrel stopped and looked at them. It said, "Sorry, but I need acorns. They are tasty and good for me. You have many acorns. Can I have some more, please?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other and smiled. They said, "Okay, you can have some more. But only if you play with us. Can you balance acorns on your head, too?"

The squirrel nodded and said, "Yes, I can. I am good at balancing. Let's play together."

Lily, Ben, and the squirrel became friends and played with the acorns. They balanced, tossed, and rolled them. They had a lot of fun and shared the acorns. They learned that acorns are not only tasty, but also fun.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a candle in a drawer. It was enormous and had many colors. They wanted to see how it looked when it was lit.

"Let's light the candle and put it on the table," Anna said.

"Okay, but we have to be careful. Mommy said candles are hot and can burn things," Ben said.

They took a match from another drawer and lit the candle. It made a bright flame and a nice smell. They put it on the table and watched it.

"It's so pretty," Anna said.

"Yes, it is. I wonder what happens if we touch it," Ben said.

He reached out his hand and touched the flame. It hurt him a lot. He screamed and pulled back his hand.

"Ow, ow, ow! It burns, it burns!" he cried.

Anna was scared and tried to help him. She grabbed a towel and wrapped it around his hand. But the towel caught fire too. It made a big smoke and a loud noise.

The smoke alarm went off and the fire sprinklers came on. The water put out the fire, but it also soaked everything in the room. The toys, the books, the clothes, everything was wet and ruined.

Mommy and Daddy heard the alarm and ran to the room. They saw the mess and the candle and the twins. They were very angry and very sad.

"What have you done? You could have been hurt or killed! Don't you know how dangerous candles are? Don't you value your lives and your things?" Mommy yelled.

"We're sorry, Mommy. We just wanted to play. We didn't know it would be so bad," Anna said.

"Sorry is not enough. You have to learn your lesson. You have to pay for the damage. You have to give up all your toys and your allowance for a long time. And you have to go to bed without dinner. Now go to your room and think about what you did," Daddy said.

He took them to their room and locked the door. They had no toys, no food, no fun. They only had each other and their pain. They cried and hugged and wished they never found the candle. They realized they made a big mistake. They wished they could go back and do things differently. But it was too late. The end.

"Wow, look at this bug!" Ben says. He picks up the beetle and holds it in his hand. "It is so big and shiny!"

"Can I see?" Lila asks. She reaches for the beetle, but Ben pulls his hand away. "No, it is mine! I found it first!"

Lila feels sad and angry. She wants to see the bug too. She tries to grab the beetle from Ben, but he twists his hand and runs away. "Stop, Ben! That is not nice!" Lila shouts.

The beetle does not like being twisted and pulled. It feels scared and hurt. It wants to go back to the garden. It bites Ben's finger with its strong jaws. "Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cries. He drops the beetle and holds his finger. "It bit me! It bit me!"

Lila runs to Ben and sees his finger. It is red and swollen. She feels sorry for Ben and the beetle. She picks up the beetle and puts it on a leaf. "I am sorry, bug. You can go now. You are free." She says.

The beetle crawls away and hides under a rock. It is happy to be safe. Lila hugs Ben and says, "I am sorry, Ben. Are you okay? You should not twist the bug. It is not obedient. It is wild."

Ben nods and says, "I am okay. I am sorry, Lila. You are right. I should not twist the bug. It is not a toy. It is a living thing."

Lila and Ben smile and say, "We are friends." They go back to the house and show their mom Ben's finger. She puts some ice and a bandage on it. She says, "You are brave, Ben. And you are kind, Lila. You both learned a lesson today. Bugs are not for twisting. They are for respecting."

Ben agreed. He put on daddy's hat and tie. Lily put on mommy's dress and necklace. They found a big box and made it their house. They put some toys inside and some outside.

They played for a while, but soon they had a problem. Lily wanted to organize the toys. She said, "We have to make our house nice and tidy. Let's put the toys in the box or on the shelf."

Ben did not want to organize the toys. He said, "No, I like the toys on the floor. They are more fun that way. Let's play with them some more."

Lily and Ben argued. They were both stubborn. They did not want to listen to each other. They got angry and sad.

Then, they heard mommy's voice. She said, "Lily, Ben, time for lunch. Come inside, please."

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They realized they did not want to fight. They wanted to be friends. They said, "Sorry" and hugged. They picked up some toys and put them in the box. They said, "We can organize the rest later. Let's go eat."

They took off mommy's and daddy's clothes and put them back. They held hands and went inside. They smiled and said, "We like to play marriage, but we like to be friends more."

Lily was a very independent girl. She liked to do things by herself, without help from anyone. She could dress herself, brush her teeth, and make her bed. She was proud of her skills.

One day, she wanted to display her art on the wall. She had made a painting of a rainbow and a sun with her crayons. She thought it was very pretty and wanted to show it to everyone. She got a chair and climbed on it. She reached for the tape and tried to stick her painting on the wall.

But she was too short. She could not reach the wall. She stretched her arm as far as she could, but she only touched the edge of the painting. She tried to balance on her toes, but she lost her grip and fell off the chair.

"Ouch!" she cried. She looked at her foot and saw a red mark on her toe. It hurt a lot. She started to cry.

Her mom heard her cry and came to see what happened. She saw Lily on the floor, holding her toe, and the painting on the chair.

"What happened, sweetie?" she asked.

"I wanted to display my art, but I fell and hurt my toe," Lily sobbed.

Her mom hugged her and kissed her toe. She said, "I'm sorry, honey. You are very independent, but sometimes you need help from others. It's okay to ask for help when you need it. I can help you display your art. Where do you want to put it?"

Lily sniffled and pointed to the wall. Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, let's do it together. Your art is very beautiful and I'm proud of you."

She lifted Lily up and helped her tape her painting on the wall. Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

"I love you too, Lily. You are my independent and brave girl."

"That's what you get for not sharing!" Ben said. He was being naughty and mean.

"OK, let's go," Anna agrees. They hold hands and step out of their room. They walk down the hall and see the living room. The big carpet is soft and colorful. It has many shapes and patterns on it.

"Wow, look at the carpet," Anna says. "It looks like a map of the world. Can you see the countries and the oceans?"

"Yes, I can," Tom says. "Let's pretend we are travelers and explore the carpet. I want to go to Africa and see the lions and the elephants."

"Me too," Anna says. "But first, let's go to Europe and see the Eiffel Tower and the Big Ben."

They start to walk on the carpet, pretending they are in different places. They make sounds and gestures to match the animals and the landmarks they see. They have a lot of fun and laugh a lot.

After a while, they are tired. They lie down on the carpet and look at the ceiling. They see a fan spinning and a lamp shining.

"I like the carpet," Tom says. "It is cozy and warm. And I like playing with you. You are my best friend."

"I like the carpet too," Anna says. "It is fun and pretty. And I like playing with you too. You are my best friend."

They smile and hug each other. They close their eyes and fall asleep on the carpet. They dream of more adventures and more places to see.

"But it looks so pretty and soft," Ben said. "I want to touch it."

He ran towards the jellyfish, but Mia grabbed his hand and pulled him back. "No, Ben, stop!" she said. "You are being silly. Listen to me, I am your big sister. I know what is good for you."

Ben did not like that. He wanted to do what he wanted. He did not like Mia telling him what to do. He started to complain. "Let me go, Mia! You are mean! You are not the boss of me! I want to touch the jellyfish!"

"Ben, stop complaining!" Mia said. "You are being naughty. You are not listening to me or mom and dad. You are making a fuss. You are ruining our fun."

They praised Mia for being a good sister and stopping him. They explained to Ben why jellyfish are dangerous and why he should never touch them. They told him to say sorry to Mia and to be more careful.

Mia smiled and forgave him. She said she was glad he was okay. She said she loved him and wanted to protect him. She said they could play together and have fun. She said they could look for other things in the water that were safe and nice.

The machine was like a big truck with a big arm and a big claw. It could lift and carry heavy things. The man who drove the machine was honest and careful. He always checked the pile before he moved it. But he did not see Tom and Lily. They were too small and hidden by the metal.

The machine came closer and closer to the pile. Tom and Lily heard the noise and felt the ground shake. They were scared and wanted to run away. But they were stuck and could not move. They cried for help.

The man heard their cries and stopped the machine. He looked around and saw them. He was shocked and sorry. He quickly got out of the machine and ran to them. He lifted them out of the pile and hugged them. He asked them if they were hurt. They said no, but they were very sorry. They did not know they were not supposed to be there.

The man was glad they were safe. He told them they were very lucky. He said the pile was very dangerous and could fall or burn or cut them. He said they should never play near the factory again. He said they should always listen to signs and adults. He said he would take them home and tell their parents.

Tom and Lily nodded and said yes. They were ashamed and scared. They thanked the man for saving them. They said he was very kind and honest. They said they would never play near the factory again. They said they would always be careful and good.

"No, Tom," Lily said. "It's dangerous. The smoke can hurt us. And the fire can burn us. We should stay here and wait for Mom and Dad."

But Tom was curious and brave. He did not listen to Lily. He raised the ball and threw it towards the smoke. He wanted to see if it would bounce back. He ran after the ball.

"Tom, come back!" Lily shouted. She was scared for Tom. She followed him.

They got to the big house. The smoke was everywhere. It made their eyes water and their throats dry. They coughed and sneezed. They saw flames and sparks. They heard people screaming and crying.

They saw their ball. It was on the ground, near the door. It was black and melted. It looked like a lump of coal.

Tom was sad. He loved his ball. He reached for it.

"Tom, don't!" Lily yelled. She saw something falling from the roof. It was a big piece of wood. It was on fire. It was coming towards Tom.

She grabbed Tom and pulled him away. They fell to the ground. The wood crashed where they were. It made a loud noise. It broke the door. It made more fire.

Tom and Lily were scared. They hugged each other. They cried.

They heard a voice. It was Mom. She had come with Dad. They had seen the smoke and the fire. They had looked for Tom and Lily. They had found them.

"Tom, Lily, are you okay?" Mom asked. She was worried. She checked them for injuries. They had some scratches and bruises. They were dirty and smelly. But they were not hurt.

"We're okay, Mom," Tom said. He was sorry. He knew he had been foolish. He had put himself and Lily in danger. He had lost his ball.

"I'm sorry, Mom," he said. "I threw my ball at the smoke. I wanted to see what would happen. I didn't mean to cause trouble."

Mom hugged Tom. She was glad he was alive. She was not angry. She understood he was curious. She was proud he was brave. But she also wanted him to be careful.

"It's okay, Tom," she said. "I'm happy you're safe. But you have to be more careful. Smoke and fire are not toys. They can hurt you and others. You have to listen to Lily. She was smart and wise. She tried to stop you. She saved you."

Tom looked at Lily. She looked at him. They smiled. They were happy they had each other. They were happy they had Mom and Dad. They were happy they were okay.

They learned a lesson. They never played with smoke and fire again. They played with other things. They had fun. They were careful. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little bunny who lived in a forest. He didn't have a lot of food to eat, and he was always scared of the big animals that lived around him. One day, the bunny saw a big tree that had fallen down. He thought to himself, "I can build a little house with this tree!"

So the bunny started to build his house with the tree. He worked very hard and it took him a long time, but finally, he had a cozy little home. He was so happy that he started to sing and dance around his new house. But then, he heard a loud noise coming from the forest. It was a big, scary bear!

The bunny was so scared that he ran into his little house and closed the door. But the bear was so big that he broke down the door and came inside. The bunny was trembling with fear, but then he remembered something. He remembered the silence of the forest at night, and how peaceful it was. So he closed his eyes and took a deep breath, and suddenly he wasn't scared anymore.

The bear saw how brave the little bunny was and he felt ashamed for being so mean. He apologized to the bunny and they became friends. From that day on, the bunny was never scared again, because he knew that he could build anything he needed to be safe, and that the silence of the forest would always bring him peace.

Ben looked at it and said, "I don't know. Maybe it is a mineral. A mineral is a thing that comes from the ground. Some minerals are hard, like rocks. Some minerals are soft, like salt."

Anna felt the white thing with her fingers. It was not hard, but it was not soft either. It was somewhere in between. She said, "Let's examine it. Maybe we can find out more about it."

They examined the white thing. They rolled it, tapped it, and smelled it. They did not see any colors, patterns, or holes on it. They did not hear any sounds, or smell any smells from it. It was just a big, round, white thing.

They decided to take it home and show it to their mom. Maybe she would know what it was. They put it in their backpack and walked to their house.

When they got home, they ran to their mom and said, "Mom, mom, look what we found in the park! It is a mineral, but we don't know what kind of mineral. Can you tell us?"

Their mom looked at the white thing and smiled. She said, "Oh, you found a pearl. A pearl is a very special kind of mineral. It is made by a sea animal called an oyster. An oyster lives in a shell, and sometimes a small thing gets inside the shell and bothers the oyster. The oyster covers the small thing with many layers of a shiny, smooth, white material. That material is called nacre. After a long time, the small thing becomes a pearl."

Anna and Ben were amazed. They said, "Wow, a pearl! That is so cool! How did it get in the park?"

Their mom said, "Maybe someone lost it, or maybe a bird dropped it. Pearls are very valuable, because they are rare and beautiful. You are very lucky to find one. But you know what is more valuable than a pearl?"

Anna and Ben shook their heads. They said, "No, what is more valuable than a pearl?"

Their mom said, "You are. You are my precious pearls. You are rare and beautiful, and I love you very much. You make me happy every day. Thank you for sharing your discovery with me."

Anna and Ben hugged their mom and said, "We love you too, mom. You are the best mom in the world. Thank you for teaching us about pearls."

The moral of the story is: Some things are more valuable than others, but nothing is more valuable than love and family.

"What is it?" Ben asked, looking up.

"Look, Ben, look!" Sara says. "There is a truck with animals. Maybe it has a lion, or a monkey, or a zebra. Let's go see them!"

"No, Sara, no!" Ben says. "We can't go outside. Mom said we have to stay in our room. The truck is not for us. Maybe the animals are fake. They are just toys, like ours."

Sara does not listen to Ben. She wants to see the animals. She runs to the door. She tries to open it. But it is locked. Mom locked the door when she went to the kitchen. Sara is angry. She cries.

"Let me out, let me out!" Sara shouts. "I want to see the animals. They are not fake. They are real. They are fun. You are mean, Ben. You don't want to play with me."

Ben feels sad. He does not want to make Sara cry. He does not want to be mean. He wants to play with her. But he also wants to obey Mom. He does not want to get in trouble. He tries to calm Sara down.

"Sara, Sara, please don't cry." Ben says. "The animals are not going anywhere. Maybe the truck will stay for a long time. Maybe we can see them later, when Mom comes back. Maybe she will let us go outside, if we are good. Please, Sara, please. Come play with me. We have many toys and books. We can have fun in our room."

Sara stops crying. She looks at Ben. She sees that he is sad too. She feels sorry. She loves Ben. He is her twin. She decides to listen to him. She goes back to the window. She looks at the truck. She sees that some of the boxes are moving. She thinks maybe Ben is right. Maybe the animals are fake. Maybe they are just toys, like theirs. She smiles.

"OK, Ben, OK." Sara says. "I will play with you. We can see the animals later. Maybe they are fake. Maybe they are real. It doesn't matter. We have each other. We are twins. We are real. We are fun."

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play with blocks. They wanted to build a big tower with all the blocks they had. They worked hard and put one block on top of another. They were happy when they saw their tower grow taller and taller.

"Look, Lily, we did it!" Tom said. "We made the biggest tower ever!"

"Yes, Tom, we succeed!" Lily said. "Our tower is a symbol of our friendship!"

But then, Ben came along. Ben was a spoiled boy who did not like to share. He saw Lily and Tom's tower and felt jealous. He wanted to have the tower for himself.

"Hey, that's my tower!" Ben shouted. "Give it to me!"

"No, Ben, it's ours!" Lily and Tom said. "We made it together!"

Ben did not listen. He pushed Lily and Tom away and grabbed the tower. He tried to take it to his corner, but the tower was too heavy and unstable. It fell down and broke into pieces. The blocks scattered everywhere.

Lily and Tom were sad and angry. They cried and shouted at Ben.

"Ben, you are mean and selfish!" Lily said. "You ruined our tower and our friendship!"

"Ben, you are stupid and greedy!" Tom said. "You did not succeed, you failed!"

Ben was also sad and angry. He did not have the tower or any friends. He threw the blocks and stomped his feet.

"Go away, Lily and Tom!" Ben said. "I don't need you or your tower!"

But no one wanted to play with Ben. He was alone and unhappy. He wished he had been nice and shared. He learned that being spoiled does not make you happy. The end.

One day, his mom says, "Tom, we have to go to the store. Put your toys away and get your coat." Tom does not want to go to the store. He wants to play with his toys. He says, "No, mom, no store. Play, play, play!"

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play with toys. One day, they found a big box of old clothes and shoes in the basement. They decided to dress up and pretend to be different people.

Lily put on a red dress and a hat with a feather. She said, "I am a princess and you are my servant. You have to do what I say."

Ben did not like that. He wanted to be a pirate and have fun. He put on a coat and a hat with a skull. He said, "No, I am a pirate and you are my prisoner. You have to give me your jewels."

They started to argue and pull each other's clothes. They did not share or listen. They were harsh and mean.

Then, they heard a loud zip sound. They looked and saw that they had ripped the coat and the dress. They also saw that the hat with the feather and the hat with the skull were stuck together with glue. They had made a big mess.

They felt sorry and ashamed. They said, "We are sorry. We were not nice. We should have played together and respected each other's choices."

They hugged and apologized. They tried to fix the clothes and the hats. They learned that being friends is more important than being right. They learned to be kind and gentle.

"OK, Mom, I will," Ben said.

"You're welcome, Lily. We're glad you enjoyed it," Dad said.

They hugged and kissed Mom and Dad, and then they went home. They dreamed of the penguin and the other animals. They wanted to go to the zoo again.

"Can we go now, mom?" Sara asked.

"Not yet, sweetie. The party starts at two o'clock. We still have some time. Why don't you play with your toys for a while?" mom said.

Sara nodded. She went to her room and played with her dolls. She pretended they were going to the party too. She made them talk and dance and sing.

Soon, it was time to go. Sara put on her pink dress and her shiny shoes. She grabbed her present and ran to the door.

"Wait, Sara. You need your coat. It's cold outside." mom said.

"No, mom. I don't need a coat. I'm not cold. I'm hot. I want to go now." Sara said.

"Sara, you have to wear a coat. You don't want to get sick, do you?" mom said.

Sara shook her head. She did not want to get sick. But she did not want to wear a coat either. She insisted.

"Please, mom. Please. No coat. No coat." Sara said.

Mom sighed. She knew Sara was stubborn. She did not want to argue with her. She wanted Sara to have fun at the party.

"Okay, Sara. No coat. But you have to promise me something. You have to stay inside the house. Don't go outside. It's too cold for you. Do you understand?" mom said.

Sara nodded. She understood. She promised.

"Thank you, mom. You're the best. I love you." Sara said.

She hugged mom and kissed her cheek. Then she ran to Ben's house. She rang the bell. Ben opened the door. He smiled.

"Hi, Sara. I'm so glad you came. Come in. The party is in the living room." Ben said.

Sara followed Ben. She saw a big cake, a lot of balloons, and many other kids. She gave Ben her present. He thanked her. They played games, ate cake, and sang songs. Sara had a lot of fun. She forgot about her coat.

But then, she felt a breeze. She looked out the window. She saw snow. It was snowing. Sara loved snow. She wanted to touch it. She wanted to make a snowman. She forgot about her promise.

She ran to the door. She opened it. She stepped outside. She felt the cold. She felt the snow. She laughed. She ran to the yard. She started to roll a snowball.

But then, she felt something else. She felt dizzy. She felt sick. She felt her nose run. She felt her throat hurt. She felt her head ache. She remembered her coat. She remembered her promise. She wished she had listened to mom. She wished she had stayed inside. She cried. She ran back to the door. She knocked. She called for mom. She wanted to go home. She wanted to be warm. She wanted to be well. She learned her lesson.

One day, a thief came to Mark's house. He wanted to take Mark's toys and books. He was not polite. He broke the window and climbed inside.

Mark was playing in his room. He heard a loud noise. He saw the thief in the hall. He was scared. He ran to his closet and hid.

The thief saw Mark's room. He saw many toys and books. He smiled. He started to put them in his bag.

Mark peeked from the closet. He saw the thief take his teddy bear. He loved his teddy bear. He was angry. He shouted, "Stop! That is my teddy bear! Give it back!"

The thief was surprised. He turned and saw Mark. He was not scared. He laughed. He said, "No, this is my teddy bear now. You are too small to stop me."

Mark was brave. He ran out of the closet. He grabbed his teddy bear from the thief. He said, "No, this is my teddy bear. You are a bad thief. Go away!"

The thief was angry. He tried to take the teddy bear back. He pushed Mark. Mark fell on the floor. He cried.

The thief heard a siren. He looked out the window. He saw a police car. He was scared. He dropped the bag and the teddy bear. He ran to the window. He tried to climb out.

But it was too late. The police came in. They saw the thief. They caught him. They said, "You are under arrest. You are a bad thief. You are not polite. You broke the window and took Mark's toys and books."

The police saw Mark. He was on the floor. He was holding his teddy bear. He was still crying. They said, "Are you okay, Mark? We are here to help you. You are a good boy. You are brave. You stopped the thief."

Mark smiled. He said, "Thank you, police. You are good. You are polite. You saved my toys and books."

The police smiled. They said, "You are welcome, Mark. We are glad you are safe. We will take the thief to jail. He will learn his lesson. He will not bother you again."

Mark hugged his teddy bear. He said, "I am happy. I have my teddy bear. I have my toys and books. I have the police. They are my friends."

Anna was sick. She had a sore throat and a fever. She did not want to play or eat. Her mom was worried. She called the doctor.

The doctor came to Anna's house. He had a bag with tools. He smiled at Anna and said, "Hello, Anna. I am here to help you feel better. Can I measure your temperature?"

Anna nodded. She opened her mouth. The doctor put a stick under her tongue. He looked at a watch. He said, "You have a high temperature, Anna. You need some medicine."

He took out a bottle and a spoon. He poured some liquid on the spoon. He said, "This is your medicine, Anna. It will make your throat less sore and your fever go away. It is yummy. It tastes like cherry. Can you try it?"

Anna looked at the spoon. She was scared. She did not like medicine. She said, "No, thank you. I don't want it."

The doctor said, "I know, Anna. Medicine is not fun. But it is good for you. It will help you heal. And it is yummy. I promise. Do you like cherry?"

Anna nodded. She liked cherry. She liked cherry ice cream and cherry juice. She said, "Yes, I like cherry."

The doctor said, "Then you will like this medicine, too. It is cherry-flavored. Just like your ice cream and juice. Can you take a sip?"

Anna looked at her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Anna. The doctor is right. The medicine is yummy. And it will make you feel better. I will take some, too. See?"

Her mom took a sip from the spoon. She said, "Mmm, yummy. Cherry. Do you want some, Anna?"

Anna nodded. She took the spoon from her mom. She put it in her mouth. She tasted the medicine. It was sweet and cherry. She said, "Mmm, yummy. Cherry."

The doctor clapped his hands. He said, "Good job, Anna. You are very brave. You took your medicine. I am proud of you. And I am sure you will feel better soon. Just rest and drink lots of water. And eat some yummy food when you are hungry."

Anna smiled. She said, "Thank you, doctor. You are very nice. And you have yummy medicine."

The doctor smiled. He said, "You are very welcome, Anna. You are very sweet. And you have a yummy smile." He gave her a sticker and a hug. He said, "Bye, Anna. Get well soon."

Anna waved. She said, "Bye, doctor. Thank you for helping me." She snuggled with her mom. She felt a little better. She closed her eyes. She dreamed of cherry ice cream and juice.

One day, Ben and Sam were playing in the park. They saw a cop on a bike. He was wearing a hat and a badge. Ben and Sam wanted to have some fun. They decided to poke the cop.

They ran behind the cop and poked him on his back. The cop turned around and looked at them. He was not happy. He said, "Hey, what are you doing? That is not nice. You should not poke people. It can hurt them or make them angry. How would you like it if someone poked you?"

Ben and Sam felt bad. They did not want to hurt the cop or make him angry. They said, "We are sorry, cop. We were just playing. We did not mean to be mean. We will not poke you again."

The cop smiled and said, "Thank you for saying sorry. I accept your apology. I know you were just playing, but you have to be careful. Poking can be dangerous. You should only poke things that are soft and safe, like pillows or toys. And you should always ask before you poke someone. Do you understand?"

Ben and Sam nodded and said, "Yes, we understand. Thank you for teaching us, cop. You are a good cop. Can we be your friends?"

The cop said, "Sure, you can be my friends. But remember, friends do not poke each other. They help each other and respect each other. That is the right way to play. Do you agree?"

Ben and Sam said, "Yes, we agree. We will be good friends. And we will not poke anyone again. We learned our lesson. Poking is silly and wrong."

The cop said, "Good. I am glad you learned your lesson. Now, go and have fun. But be careful and kind. And if you ever need me, just call me. I am here to help you and protect you. That is what cops do."

Ben and Sam said, "Thank you, cop. You are the best. Bye!"

They waved at the cop and ran to play with their toys. They did not poke anyone again. They were happy and good. They learned that poking is silly and wrong, and that being kind and respectful is the right way to play.

Tim and Sam are two dogs who like to play together. They run, jump, bark and chase each other in the park. One day, they find a big bone under a tree. It smells good and looks tasty.

"Wow, look at this bone!" Tim says. "It is so big and hard. I want to bite it."

"Me too!" Sam says. "Let's share it. You can have one end and I can have the other."

They both grab the bone and start to pull. They tug and tug, but the bone does not break. They growl and snarl, but the bone does not move. They are both very strong and stubborn.

"Let go of the bone!" Tim says. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Sam says. "You let go!"

They keep pulling and pulling, until they hear a loud crack. The bone breaks in half. They both fall back and drop their pieces. They look at each other and feel silly.

"Oops, we broke the bone," Tim says. "Now it is not so big and hard."

"Maybe we should not have pulled so hard," Sam says. "Now it is not so tasty."

They both sigh and look at their pieces. They are small and soft. They do not smell good or look tasty. They are not fun to bite.

"Maybe we can find another bone," Tim says. "A bigger and better one."

Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy some oranges. As they were walking home, they saw the same big, scary dog. This time, the dog was not playing. He was angry and barking loudly. Lily was very scared and started to cry. 

Suddenly, the dog jumped and bit Lily's leg. Lily's mom called for help, but it was too late. Lily had to go to the hospital and get a lot of stitches. From that day on, Lily was scared of dogs and never wanted to go to the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a daddy. They had a daughter who was very small but very smart. She loved to play and run around. One day, they went to the park and saw a huge slide. The daughter was scared to go down it but her mommy and daddy helped her. They went down the slide together and it was so much fun!

The daughter wanted to go down the slide again and again. But she was still scared. Her mommy and daddy told her that if she kept trying, she would improve and not be scared anymore. So the daughter went down the slide again and again until she wasn't scared anymore. She was so happy and proud of herself. And her mommy and daddy were proud of her too. The end.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park. He loved to play on the swings and slide down the slide. While he was playing, he saw something unusual. It was a big dinosaur! 

Timmy was scared, but the dinosaur said, "Don't be afraid, little boy. I won't hurt you. I just want to stand here and look around." 

Timmy asked the dinosaur, "Why are you here? Don't you live in the jungle?" 

The dinosaur replied, "Yes, I do. But I wanted to see what the city is like. It's very different from the jungle. I like to stand here and watch the people." 

Timmy was amazed. He had never seen a dinosaur before. He said, "Wow, you're really cool! Can I stand next to you and take a picture?" 

The dinosaur smiled and said, "Of course, little boy. Let's stand together and take a picture." And so they did. Timmy was so happy to have a picture with the unusual dinosaur.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and meet new friends. One day, she met a boy named Timmy. He was sitting on a seat in the park, looking sad. 

Lily asked, "Why are you sad?" 

Timmy replied, "I lost my toy car and can't find it." 

Lily said, "I'll help you find it!" 

They searched and searched, but they couldn't find the toy car. Timmy became stubborn and refused to keep looking. 

Lily said, "Let's keep looking, we'll find it!" 

But Timmy didn't want to listen. He went home and Lily went home too. The next day, Lily went back to the park and saw Timmy crying. She asked him what was wrong and he said he found his toy car, but it was broken. 

Lily felt sad too and said, "I'm sorry we couldn't find it yesterday." 

Timmy said, "It's okay, I'm just sad it's broken." 

Lily gave Timmy a hug and they both felt a little better.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play basketball. He had a big, thick ball that he would dribble around all day.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play basketball. He saw his friend Billy there and they started to play together. They laughed and had fun, but then it started to rain.

Billy said, "I think we should go home now." But Timmy said, "Just one more shot!" He threw the ball, but it slipped out of his hands and went into the street. Timmy ran after it, but a car came and he got hit. Timmy's family and friends were very sad because they would miss him and his love for basketball.

Her mom said, "Let's go find a place where it's cool." So, they went to the park where there was a big tree with lots of shade. They sat down and ate some yummy fruit.

After a while, Lily saw a little boy crying. She went up to him and asked, "What's wrong?" The little boy said, "I lost my toy." So, Lily helped him find it. When they found the toy, the little boy was very happy and said, "Thank you, Lily!"

Lily learned that helping others can make you happy too. From that day on, she always tried to help people whenever she could.

Lily was sad because she didn't know it was wrong to keep something that didn't belong to her. She learned her lesson and promised to always do the right thing.

Once upon a time, there was a big, beautiful flower. It was pink and had many petals. A little girl saw it and wanted it very much. She asked the flower seller, "How much is it?" The seller said, "The price is five coins." The little girl didn't have enough coins, so she went home sad.

The next day, the little girl came back to see the flower. But to her surprise, the flower had shrunk! It was now small and not as beautiful as before. The seller said, "Now the price is only one coin." The little girl was happy because she could afford it. She gave the seller one coin and took the small flower home. She put it in a vase and it still looked beautiful to her.

Lily was a shy girl who did not like to talk in front of the class. She liked to draw and write on her blackboard at home, but she was afraid to show her work to anyone. She had a secret wish to be a teacher when she grew up, but she did not think she could do it.

One day, her teacher asked her to help with a special project. She wanted Lily to draw some pictures on the big blackboard in the classroom, and then explain them to the other children. Lily felt nervous and scared. She wanted to say no, but she also wanted to make her teacher happy. She decided to accept the challenge and try her best.

She worked hard on her drawings, using different colors and shapes. She drew a sun, a flower, a house, a cat, and a book. She practiced what she would say in her head, over and over. She hoped the other children would like her pictures and not laugh at her.

The next day, it was time to present her project. She walked up to the front of the class, holding her chalk. She looked at the big blackboard, and then at the faces of her classmates. She felt her heart beat fast and her mouth go dry. She wanted to run away, but she remembered her teacher's smile and her own wish. She took a deep breath and started to talk.

She pointed to each picture and said its name. She told the class what she liked about each one, and why she drew it. She spoke slowly and softly, but clearly and confidently. She looked at the other children and saw that they were listening and smiling. They clapped and cheered when she finished. She felt a warm and happy feeling in her chest. She had done it. She had shared her work and her voice with the class. She had been brave and proud. She had been a teacher.

Anna liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She wanted to learn how to cook and bake. Mom said that cooking and baking were important jobs. She said that if Anna wanted to be a good cook and baker, she had to prepare well.

One day, mom asked Anna to help her make a cake for dad's birthday. Anna was very happy. She wanted to make a yummy cake for dad. She followed mom's instructions and helped her measure, mix, and pour the ingredients. She also helped her decorate the cake with frosting and sprinkles.

When the cake was ready, mom and Anna put it in a big box and took it to the living room. They waited for dad to come home from work. Anna was very excited. She wanted to see dad's face when he saw the cake.

Soon, dad came home. He hugged mom and Anna and thanked them for the cake. He said it looked delicious and beautiful. He cut a big slice and tasted it. He smiled and said it was the best cake he ever had. He praised Anna for her help and said she was a successful baker.

Anna felt very proud and happy. She learned that preparing well was the key to doing a good job. She also learned that helping mom and dad was a way of showing love. She hugged dad and mom and said she loved them very much. They hugged her back and said they loved her too. They enjoyed the cake together and had a wonderful birthday celebration.

Lily likes to mix colors. She has many paints and brushes. She puts some red and yellow on a paper. She mixes them and makes orange. She smiles and says, "Orange is a bright color. I like orange."

She sees a parrot on a tree outside. The parrot has many bright colors too. It has red, yellow, green and blue feathers. It looks at Lily and says, "Hello, hello!" Lily is surprised and happy. She says, "Hello, parrot! You are very pretty. Can I paint you?"

The parrot flies to Lily's window. It says, "Yes, yes! Paint me, paint me!" Lily takes her paints and brushes. She paints the parrot on another paper. She mixes the colors to make the parrot's feathers. She says, "You are a rainbow parrot. You have all the colors."

The parrot looks at the painting. It says, "Wow, wow! You are a good painter. You made me look like a rainbow. Thank you, thank you!" Lily and the parrot are both happy. They become friends and talk and play. Lily likes to mix colors and the parrot likes to talk. They have fun together.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big teddy bear and Ben had a small car. They were having fun and sharing nicely.

But then Ben saw Lily's teddy bear and wanted to play with it. He asked Lily, "Can I have your teddy bear, please?"

Lily said, "No, this is my teddy bear. You have your car."

Ben was angry and did not listen. He grabbed the teddy bear from Lily and ran away. Lily was sad and chased him.

"Give me back my teddy bear!" she cried.

Ben did not want to give it back. He held the teddy bear tightly and bit its ear. He thought it would make Lily go away.

But the teddy bear was not happy. It felt pain and did not like Ben. It bit Ben back on his hand. Ben screamed and dropped the teddy bear.

Lily picked up her teddy bear and hugged it. She checked its ear and said, "I'm sorry, teddy bear. Are you okay?"

The teddy bear nodded and smiled. It was glad that Lily was kind and gentle.

Ben looked at his hand and saw blood. He felt pain and was scared. He ran to his mom and said, "Mom, mom, the teddy bear bit me!"

His mom saw his wound and said, "Oh, Ben, what did you do? You should not bite toys. They can bite you back. Come, let me clean your hand and put a band-aid on it."

She took Ben to the bathroom and washed his hand. She put some cream and a band-aid on it. She said, "There, there, it will be better soon. You need to be calm and say sorry to Lily and the teddy bear. They are your friends, not your enemies."

Ben nodded and felt sorry. He went back to the living room and said to Lily and the teddy bear, "I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, teddy bear. I was wrong to bite you. Can we be friends again?"

Lily and the teddy bear forgave Ben and said, "Yes, we can be friends again. But you have to be nice and share."

Ben agreed and said, "Okay, I will be nice and share. Can I play with your car, Lily?"

Lily said, "Sure, you can play with my car. And I can play with your teddy bear. We can take turns."

They smiled and played together happily. They learned their lesson and did not bite anyone or anything again.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. Sometimes they share, sometimes they fight. One day, they find a big bag of rice in the kitchen. They think it is fun to pour the rice on the floor and make shapes with it.

"Look, I made a star!" Sara says, showing Ben her rice star.

"I made a car!" Ben says, showing Sara his rice car.

They play with the rice for a while, until their mom comes in. She is not happy. She sees the mess on the floor and the empty bag of rice.

"What are you doing?" she asks, in a loud voice. "This is not fake rice, this is real rice. We need it for dinner. You wasted it all!"

Sara and Ben feel bad. They did not know the rice was real. They thought it was fake, like their other toys.

"Sorry, mom," they say, in a small voice.

Mom sighs. She is not very angry, but she is tired. She tells Sara and Ben to help her clean up the rice. She gives them a broom and a dustpan.

"Separate the rice from the dirt," she says. "Put the rice in this bowl, and the dirt in the trash. Maybe we can still use some of the rice for dinner."

Sara and Ben do what mom says. They separate the rice from the dirt. They work hard and fast. They fill the bowl with rice and the trash with dirt. They say sorry to mom again.

Mom smiles. She hugs Sara and Ben. She says she loves them, even when they make mistakes. She says they can still have rice for dinner, but they have to be careful next time. She says they can play with fake rice, but not with real rice.

Sara and Ben nod. They understand. They say they love mom too. They say they will be careful next time. They say they will play with fake rice, but not with real rice.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big gray box near the trees. They were curious and went to look.

The box had a hole on one side. Tom and Lily peeked inside. They saw many masks. The masks had different colors and shapes. Some looked like animals, some looked like people, some looked like monsters.

Tom and Lily wanted to try the masks. They took some out of the box and put them on their faces. They laughed and pretended to be the masks. They did not see the sign on the box that said "Do not touch. These masks are for a show."

A man came out of the trees. He was angry. He saw Tom and Lily with the masks. He shouted at them. He said they were bad and they destroyed his masks. He said the masks were very special and expensive. He said he worked hard to make them. He said he would tell their parents.

Tom and Lily were scared. They took off the masks and tried to run away. But the man was faster. He grabbed them and took them to his car. He said he would keep them until their parents paid for the masks. He said they would be sorry. He locked them in the car and drove away.

Tom and Lily cried. They wished they never touched the masks. They wished they stayed on the slide, the swing and the run. They did not know what would happen to them. They were in trouble. They were very sad. The end.

Timmy did not like cauliflower. He thought it was white and yucky and smelled bad. He always left it on his plate when Mommy gave it to him for dinner. But Mommy said he had to eat it or he would not get any dessert.

One day, Timmy had a plan. He saw a big bowl of cauliflower on the kitchen table. He sneaked over and took some in his hand. He ran outside and threw it in the trash can. He did this again and again until the bowl was empty. He smiled and went back inside.

"Timmy, are you ready for dinner?" Mommy called.

"Yes, Mommy!" Timmy said. He sat down at the table and watched Mommy bring the food. He saw mashed potatoes, chicken, and...cauliflower!

"Where did you get more cauliflower, Mommy?" Timmy asked.

"I didn't, Timmy. This is the same cauliflower from the bowl. I just washed it and cooked it. Why do you ask?" Mommy said.

Timmy felt sick. He remembered throwing the cauliflower in the trash can. He remembered seeing flies and dirt and worms on it. He realized he had spoiled the cauliflower and Mommy had cooked it anyway.

"Mommy, I have to tell you something..." Timmy said. He started to cry. He wished he had eaten the cauliflower when it was fresh and clean. He learned a lesson that day. He never threw away food again.

One day, they find a new toy in the box. It is a motor. It is shiny and red. It has a switch and a wire. Tom and Lily do not know what it does. They are curious.

"Let's play with the motor," Tom says.

"OK, but how?" Lily asks.

"Maybe we can make it move something," Tom says. He looks around the room. He sees a car. He picks it up. He tries to attach the wire to the car. He flips the switch. Nothing happens.

"Maybe it needs batteries," Lily says. She remembers that their dad has some batteries in his drawer. She runs to get them. She brings them back to Tom. Tom puts the batteries in the motor. He flips the switch again. The motor makes a loud noise. It spins very fast. The wire flies off the car. It hits Tom in the face. It hurts.

"Ow!" Tom cries. He drops the motor. He rubs his face. He feels something wet on his tongue. It is blood. It is bitter. He does not like it.

"Are you OK, Tom?" Lily asks. She is worried. She hugs Tom. She gives him a tissue. She helps him clean his face.

"I'm OK, Lily," Tom says. He smiles. He is brave. He does not cry. He hugs Lily back. He thanks her.

"Let's not play with the motor anymore," Lily says.

"OK, let's play with something else," Tom says.

They put the motor back in the box. They prepare to play with their dolls. They are happy. They are twins. They love each other.

Lily and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy.

But then, a mean boy came by. He kicked the snowman and broke his nose. He laughed and said, "Your snowman is ugly and silly. I can make a better one."

Lily and Ben were very sad and angry. They shouted, "Stop it! You are mean and bad. Go away!"

The mean boy did not listen. He said, "No, I will not go away. I will make a spell and turn you into snowmen too. Then I will kick you and break you."

He took a stick and waved it in the air. He said some words that Lily and Ben did not understand. He said, "Now you are snowmen. Ha ha ha!"

Lily and Ben felt very cold and stiff. They could not move or talk. They were scared. They started to shiver.

But then, a big dog came by. He saw the mean boy and barked. He ran towards him and bit his leg. The mean boy screamed and dropped the stick. He ran away, crying.

The dog picked up the stick and brought it to Lily and Ben. He wagged his tail and licked their faces. He was a friendly dog.

Lily and Ben felt warm and soft again. They could move and talk. They were not snowmen anymore. They were happy.

They hugged the dog and thanked him. They said, "You are a good and brave dog. You saved us from the mean boy. You broke his spell."

The dog barked and smiled. He said, "You are welcome. You are nice and kind. You made a beautiful snowman. You are healthy."

Lily and Ben smiled too. They said, "You are right. We are healthy. And we are friends. Do you want to play with us?"

The dog nodded and wagged his tail. He said, "Yes, I do. Let's play in the snow."

They played in the snow until it was dark. They had a lot of fun. They were happy.

Sara and Ben like to play with water. They have a big hose in the garden. They can spray water from the hose. They spray water on the flowers, on the grass, and on each other. They laugh and have fun.

One day, they decide to build a bridge with some sticks and stones. They find a good spot near the pond. They work hard to make the bridge strong and pretty. They are proud of their bridge.

They want to spray water on their bridge. They think it will look nice and shiny. They run to the hose and turn it on. But the hose is too short. They cannot reach the bridge with the water.

They see a man walking by. He has a big bucket of water. He is going to water his plants. Sara and Ben have an idea. They run to the man and ask him politely:

"Excuse me, sir. Can we borrow your bucket of water? We want to spray water on our bridge. We made it ourselves. It is over there, near the pond. Please, sir. Can we?"

The man smiles. He likes Sara and Ben. He thinks they are clever and polite. He says:

"Sure, you can borrow my bucket of water. But be careful. Don't spill it. And don't spray water on anyone who doesn't want to. OK?"

Sara and Ben say:

"OK, sir. Thank you, sir. You are very kind."

They take the bucket of water and run to their bridge. They spray water on their bridge. They make it look nice and shiny. They are happy. They thank the man again and give him back his bucket. The man says:

"You're welcome, Sara and Ben. You have a lovely bridge. You are good builders. And you are good sharers. Well done."

Sara and Ben smile. They hug the man. They say:

"Thank you, sir. You are a good friend. Goodbye, sir."

They wave to the man and go back to their bridge. They play with water some more. They have a wonderful day.

Lily was playing with her toy car in the garden. She liked to make it zoom and beep on the grass. She saw a big fly buzzing near a flower. She wanted to catch it and look at it. She ran after the fly with her car.

"Come here, fly!" she said. "I want to see you!"

But the fly was too fast and clever. It flew away from Lily and her car. It landed on a leaf and laughed.

"Ha ha, you can't catch me!" it said. "You are too big and slow!"

Lily felt angry and sad. She wished she was small and fast like the fly. She saw a bottle on the ground. It had a label that said "Shrink". She did not know what that meant, but she thought it might help her. She opened the bottle and drank some of the liquid.

Suddenly, she felt very strange. She looked at her car and saw that it was much bigger than her. She looked at her hands and saw that they were very tiny. She had shrunk!

She heard the fly laughing again.

"Look at you, you are smaller than me!" it said. "Now I can catch you and eat you!"

Lily was scared. She did not want to be eaten by the fly. She ran away from the leaf and looked for a place to hide. She saw a hole in the ground. She ran inside and hoped the fly would not find her.

But the hole was dark and cold. She could not see anything. She heard a loud noise and felt something moving. It was a worm!

"Who are you?" the worm said. "Why are you in my home?"

Lily was more scared. She did not want to be eaten by the worm either. She said sorry to the worm and tried to get out of the hole. But the worm blocked her way.

"You can't leave, you are my guest!" the worm said. "And I am hungry!"

Lily cried. She wished she had not drunk the shrink liquid. She wished she was big and fast again. She wished she had left the fly alone. She wished she was back in the garden with her car. She did not like this adventure at all.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Sara has a new cell. It is shiny and can make sounds. Ben wants to see the cell, but Sara says no.

"Please, Sara, let me see your cell. It looks fun," Ben says.

"No, Ben, it is mine. You have your own toys. Go away," Sara says.

Ben is sad and angry. He waits for Sara to look away. Then he takes the cell and runs. Sara sees him and shouts.

"Ben, give me back my cell! That is not nice. You are a bad friend," Sara says.

Ben runs to his room and locks the door. He plays with the cell, but he feels guilty. He knows he did wrong. He hears Sara knock on the door.

"Ben, please open the door. I am sorry I was mean to you. I will share my cell with you. But you have to give it back. It is not yours," Sara says.

Ben thinks for a while. He knows Sara is right. He opens the door and gives back the cell. He says sorry to Sara.

"Sara, I am sorry I took your cell. That was not nice. You are a good friend. Can we still play together?" Ben says.

Sara smiles and hugs Ben. She says sorry to him too.

"Ben, I am sorry I was not patient with you. That was not nice. You are a good friend. Yes, we can still play together. And we can share my cell sometimes," Sara says.

They go to the living room and play with the cell and other toys. They are happy and learn to be patient and kind.

The moral value of the story is: Do not take what is not yours. Be patient and kind with your friends. Share and forgive.

Dad comes with Anna and sees Lily. He says Lily is sick and needs a vet. A vet is a doctor for animals. Dad calls the vet on his phone and waits for him to come. Anna stays with Lily and talks to her softly. She hopes Lily will be okay.

The vet arrives and checks Lily. He says Lily has a fever and a pain in her belly. He gives Lily some medicine and a purple bandage. The purple bandage is to help Lily feel better. The vet says Lily needs to rest and drink a lot of water. He says Lily will be fine in a few days.

Anna is happy to hear that Lily will be fine. She thanks the vet and hugs her dad. She gives Lily a kiss and a carrot. She tells Lily she loves her and will come back tomorrow. Lily opens her eyes and nuzzles Anna. Anna smiles and says goodbye to Lily. She walks with her dad to the car. She is not worried anymore. She knows Lily is in good hands.

Sara loved her kitten, Max. He was soft and warm and liked to play with her. He was an ordinary kitten, but Sara thought he was special. She liked to put him in her dollhouse and pretend he was a baby.

One day, Sara's mom had to go to the store. She told Sara to stay inside and not open the door to anyone. Sara said okay and hugged her mom. She went to play with Max in her room.

She put him in the dollhouse and gave him a bottle. She said, "You are a good baby, Max. I love you." Max meowed and licked her face. He was happy.

But then, Sara heard a knock on the door. She wondered who it was. She left Max in the dollhouse and went to see. She opened the door and saw a man. He had a big bag and a mean smile.

He said, "Hello, little girl. I have some candy for you. Do you want some?" Sara liked candy. She said, "Yes, please." She took a step outside.

The man grabbed her and put her in his bag. He said, "You are coming with me, little girl. I have a nice place for you." He ran to his car and drove away.

Sara screamed and cried. She wanted her mom and Max. She was scared.

Max heard Sara scream. He jumped out of the dollhouse and ran to the door. He saw the car drive away. He meowed and scratched the door. He wanted Sara back. He was sad.

But no one came. Max was alone. He waited and waited. He was hungry and thirsty. He was cold and tired. He was sick.

He curled up on the floor and closed his eyes. He wished he was with Sara. He wished he was an ordinary kitten. He died.

Anna and Ben were going to the lake with their mom and dad. They had to pack some things in a big bag. Anna packed her hat, her ball, and her doll. Ben packed his cap, his car, and his book.

"Are we ready?" Mom asked.

"Yes, we are!" Anna and Ben said.

They got in the car and drove to the lake. It was a sunny day and the water was blue. They saw many birds and fish. They also saw a big white swan. The swan was swimming alone. It looked sad.

"Why is the swan sad?" Anna asked.

"I don't know, maybe it lost its friend," Ben said.

"Can we be its friend?" Anna asked.

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. Swans can be angry sometimes," Ben said.

They got out of the car and walked to the shore. They saw some bread on a bench. They took some bread and threw it to the swan. The swan came closer and ate the bread. It looked happy.

"Hello, swan. We are Anna and Ben. Do you want to play with us?" Anna said.

The swan nodded and made a soft sound. It followed them to the grass. They played catch with the ball, raced with the car, and read the book. The swan liked them. It was not sad anymore.

"Look, mom and dad. The swan is our friend now. It is not troubled anymore," Ben said.

Mom and dad smiled. They were glad that Anna and Ben made a new friend. They had a fun day at the lake. They packed their things and said goodbye to the swan. The swan waved with its wing and made a loud sound. It was happy.

Lily and Ben were twins. They liked to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they fought over the toys. One day, Lily wanted to play with the doll that Ben had. She tried to grab it from him, but he held it tight.

"No, this is mine!" Ben said. "You have your own doll!"

"But I like this one better!" Lily said. "Your doll is cheap and ugly!"

Lily pulled harder, and Ben pulled harder too. They both fell on the floor, and the doll's head came off. They looked at the broken doll and started to cry.

"Look what you did!" Ben said. "You broke my doll!"

"It's your fault!" Lily said. "You wouldn't share!"

They were both very angry and sad. They did not want to talk to each other. They went to their beds and turned away.

Mom heard them crying and came to their room. She saw the broken doll and the twins' faces. She felt sorry for them.

"What happened, my loves?" Mom asked. "Why are you crying?"

Lily and Ben told Mom what happened. They both blamed each other for the doll. Mom listened and nodded.

"I see," Mom said. "It's not nice to fight over toys. You should share and take turns. And you should not say mean things to each other. You are twins, and you should love each other."

Mom picked up the doll's head and the body. She took a sock from the drawer and wrapped it around the doll's neck. She tied a knot and made a scarf.

"Look, now the doll has a new scarf!" Mom said. "She is not cheap and ugly, she is warm and cozy. And she still loves you both. Do you want to play with her?"

Lily and Ben looked at the doll. She did look warm and cozy. They felt sorry for breaking her and hurting each other.

"Can we play with her, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Of course, my loves," Mom said. "But first, you need to do something. You need to forgive each other. Can you do that?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They remembered how much they liked to play together. They did not want to be angry and sad anymore.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I should have shared with you."

"I'm sorry, Ben," Lily said. "I should not have said your doll was cheap and ugly."

They hugged each other and said, "I forgive you."

Mom smiled and hugged them too. She gave them the doll and said, "That's my good twins. Now you can play nicely with your doll. And remember, toys are fun, but love is more important."

Lily and Ben nodded and thanked Mom. They took the doll and played with her on the floor. They shared and took turns. They said nice things to each other. They were happy and loved.

"Can we make spaghetti, Anna? Please, please, please?" Lily says.

"Okay, Lily, but you have to listen to me. Making spaghetti is not easy. You need a big pot, water, salt, noodles, cheese and sauce. And you need to be careful with the stove. It is very hot," Anna says.

Lily nods. She and Anna go to the kitchen. They fill the big pot with water and put it on the stove. Anna turns on the stove and adds some salt. She tells Lily to wait until the water boils.

Lily is impatient. She wants to make spaghetti now. She sees the noodles on the counter. She thinks they look like worms. She grabs a handful of noodles and throws them into the pot.

"Stop, Lily, stop! You can't do that! The water is not boiling yet. The noodles will stick together and be mushy. And you are making a mess!" Anna shouts.

Lily looks at the pot. She sees the noodles floating in the water. They do not look like spaghetti. They look like wet worms. She feels embarrassed. She starts to cry.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I just wanted to make spaghetti. I didn't know," Lily says.

Anna sighs. She turns off the stove and takes the pot off. She hugs Lily and wipes her tears.

"It's okay, Lily. You tried to help. But you have to listen to me next time. Making spaghetti is not a game. It is a skill. Maybe we can try again another day. For now, let's clean up the kitchen and order some pizza. How does that sound?" Anna says.

Lily smiles. She likes pizza too. She says sorry to Anna again. She and Anna clean up the kitchen and call for pizza. They hope mommy and daddy will not be mad. They hope they will like pizza. They hope they will still love them.

She wanted to open them and see the shiny pearls, but her mom and dad said no. They said oysters were alive and they needed to stay in the water.

One day, Anna found a very big oyster on the sand. She was curious and picked it up. She tried to open it with her fingers, but it was too hard. She looked around and saw a rock. She thought she could use the rock to open the oyster. She carried the oyster and the rock to a quiet spot, away from her mom and dad.

"Please don't hurt me," the voice said.

"Who are you?" Anna asked.

"I'm sorry, oyster," she said. "I hope you find your family and friends."
